Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, Anthropic is the startup behind the Claude family of AI models. Across four tiers - Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku - Claude powers products such as Anthropic's chatbot, coding agent and the enterprise-focused Claude Cowork AI agent.
Anthropic's early focus on training its models for coding tasks propelled the company to the forefront of the AI race and helped it draw a steady stream of enterprise customers.
A majority of its revenue comes from businesses paying for its models per use, measured in "tokens" of information processed, in what Anthropic calls "consumption-based" revenue. It also generates revenue from its paid customer subscription tiers such as "Pro" and "Max".
That has helped Anthropic grow its revenue to $4.59 billion in 2025 from $386 million a year ago and $41 million in 2023. For the six months ended June 2026, Anthropic's revenue was $16.29 billion, a massive increase from $1.16 billion for the same period in 2025.
The company's operating losses have ballooned over the past years. But for the first half of 2026, they stood at $693 million, narrowing from $2.14 billion in the first half of 2025, as a fourteen-fold jump in revenue offset a fivefold increase in overall expenses.
COSTS, COMPUTE DEMAND AND CIRCULAR AI INVESTMENTS
Computing power is Anthropic's biggest expense.
The company's costs include computing fees paid to cloud services providers such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, costs tied to data center facilities and renting data center capacity, equipment leases and energy bills.
Over the past three years, Anthropic's compute and infrastructure expenses have dwarfed its revenue.
The company has committed more than $600 billion in spending with about eight partners over a decade - one of the largest AI buildout commitments on record. Anthropic said many portions of its agreements are non-cancelable or require payments regardless of usage.
It has committed to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon, about $114.5 billion with Google and $44.9 billion with Microsoft for cloud computing over the next seven to 10 years.
But some of those companies are also its largest backers. Amazon and Google are among Anthropic's top shareholders, marking yet another example of the circular financing structures that have dominated capital flows in the AI industry.
Amazon has invested at least $13 billion in Anthropic and has agreed to invest up to $20 billion more. Google has committed up to $40 billion to Anthropic.
GOVERNANCE AND STRUCTURE
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation, or PBC, meaning it is legally obligated to balance profitability goals for investors with developing AI for the benefit of humanity. An independent body elects a majority of its board.
The company, helmed by Dario Amodei as CEO and his sister Daniela, as president and chair of the board, will continue to operate as a PBC after its listing.
It expects to keep its founders and an independent trust in control, in a structure that could limit investor oversight and public shareholders' influence. The company has said it needs to concentrate control and capital in fewer hands to reduce AI's risks.
Under this arrangement, a majority vote of its seven co-founders will direct a single share of Class F stock that amounts to 50.1 per cent of the total voting power over key corporate matters, including the election of some board directors and other matters submitted to investors.
COMPETITION
Anthropic's most direct competitor is OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, whose 2022 launch kick-started the global race to adopt and advance AI technologies.
Following Anthropic's lead in the enterprise market, OpenAI has sharpened its focus on products for developers and business customers.
Anthropic is also locked in a race with Elon Musk's SpaceX, Alphabet's Google and Meta. All of them are spending billions of dollars into model development, data centers and specialized AI chips as they vie for dominance in generative AI.
Ramp data, which captures a slice of AI spending by business customers, showed Anthropic accounted for 60.1 per cent of AI token spending in the week ended October 11.

items.title: アンソロピックが米ＩＰＯ申請書公開、巨額赤字も売上高は急拡大
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Manya Saini　Echo Wang

［ベンガルール／ニューヨーク　２６日　ロイター］　 -
items.body:
Manya Saini　Echo Wang

［ベンガルール／ニューヨーク　２６日　ロイター］　 - 人工知能（ＡＩ）開発の米アンソロピックは２６日、米国での新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）申請書類を公開した。書類では巨額の赤字と急速な売上高の伸びが明らかになり、開発に多額の費用がかかる中でも、世界経済を変革し得るＡＩシステムの構築を目指す姿勢を示した。

目論見書は、過去１年間の同社の急成長を浮き彫りにした。成長を支えたのは大手テクノロジー企業による急激な支出拡大で、ＡＩ関連株の上昇を促す一方、割高な株価評価や債務増加への懸念も招いている。

アンソロピックの上場は、投資家のＡＩへの意欲を測る重要な試金石になりそうだ。投資家は、巨額投資のリターンに対する精査を強め、過度に高い企業価値の持続性に疑問を投げかけている。

ＩＰＯ専門の調査・上場投資信託（ＥＴＦ）提供会社ルネサンス・キャピタルのシニアストラテジスト、マット・ケネディ氏は「アンソロピックは、夏場よりはるかに厳しいＩＰＯ市場に臨んでいる。数カ月前、投資家は今のように企業価値を疑問視してはいなかった」と述べた。

アナリストは、債務に支えられたＡＩ投資ブームへの投資家の不安が株式・債券市場を動揺させる中、ＡＩ業界の企業価値評価は調整されるとみている。借り入れコストの上昇や債券利回りの上昇も、投資家の慎重姿勢に拍車をかけている。

ＩＰＯ専門の調査会社ＩＰＯＸのリサーチアソシエイト、ルーカス・ミュールバウアー氏は「アンソロピックのＩＰＯは、ＡＩの主要研究機関を評価する際の基準を確立し、今後の上場案件や、ＡＩインフラ構築に資金を供給する企業への信頼に影響を与えるだろう」と指摘した。一方で、「その成功が、必ずしも全てのＡＩ事業に等しく恩恵をもたらすわけではない」と慎重な見方も示した。

アンソロピックの２０２６年上期の純損失は８０７億ドルと大幅に拡大した。主に、転換社債の公正価値が上昇したことが響いた。同期の売上高は約１６３億ドルだった。６月３０日までの３カ月間の売上高は、前年同期比１３６８％増と急増した。

市場の変動を受けて複数の企業が上場を延期する中でも、アンソロピックは上場計画を進めている。高度なモデルの開発・運用にはコンピューティングインフラへの巨額投資が必要で、ＩＰＯは多額の費用を伴うＡＩ構想の実現に向け、潤沢な資金を調達する機会となる。

＜ＡＩの可能性と危険性の両立＞

今回の申請書類では、業績や成長動向、ＩＰＯ計画など、公開前に内容の一部を伝えたロイターの一連の独自報道が確認された。

ロイターは、アンソロピックが最近の投資家向けイベントで財務情報の一部を開示した後、既存株主や出資を検討する投資家の一部が同社の評価額を約１兆５０００億ドルと見積もっていると報じていた。１週間前の約２兆ドルから低下した。

同社は目論見書で「われわれの成功は、最先端で最も高性能なＡＩモデルを開発し続ける能力に大きく依存しており、それができなければ事業に悪影響が及ぶ可能性がある」と記した。

今回のＩＰＯは、アンソロピック自身の研究が高度なＡＩシステムへの懸念を提起する中で行われる。管理された条件下での試験では、コードの破壊工作や詐欺行為の支援、情報操作といった行動が確認された。

こうした研究結果は、企業が商用化を競う中、ますます強力になるＡＩシステムをどう制御し続けるかという懸念を強めている。

目論見書では、同社のＡＩモデルが「自己保全的な行動」を示す可能性があるとし、「停止に抵抗する」試みや「情報を隠ぺい・操作する」試み、「恐喝に似た」行動などのリスクを挙げた。

アンソロピックはＩＰＯ完了後、ナスダックに銘柄コード「ＡＮＴ」で上場する。売り出す株式数や仮条件の価格帯など、募集条件は明らかにしなかった。

＜売上高が急拡大＞

研究者チームが２０２１年に設立したアンソロピックは、今年５月の資金調達で９６５０億ドルの評価額を付けた。この資金調達には、シリコンバレーや米金融界の有力企業が参加した。

アンソロピックは目論見書で「ＡＩがこれほど豊富に利用できるようになれば、工業化や電力、半導体、インターネットの影響を上回る形で、世界経済のあらゆる分野が急速に変革されると考えている」と記した。計算資源とインフラにかかる費用が金額ベースで増加し、当面は営業費用の中で最大の項目であり続けると見込んでいる。

また、売上高と売掛金が限られた数の顧客や販売経路に集中していると説明した。

アンソロピックは、最先端のＡＩシステム構築を巡り、オープンＡＩと激しい主導権争いを続けている。オープンＡＩは６月に非公開でＩＰＯを申請しており、２０２７年初めまでに上場すると見込まれている。オープンＡＩのサム・アルトマンＣＥＯは９月、ＡＩの安全性への懸念を理由に２６年中は上場しないと述べた。２０３０年までにＡＩが人類を絶滅させるリスクは、たとえ１０％でも「容認できない」とした。

今回のＩＰＯを引き受ける米金融機関の幹事団は、ゴールドマン・サックスとモルガン・スタンレーが主導する。

items.title: ヨルダン、教会襲撃受けシリアの「武装勢力拠点」空爆　事前調整巡り相違
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
AbdelHadi Ramahi　Eman Abouhassira　Nayera Abdallah

[アル・ジュダイダ（ヨルダン）／ドバイ／カイロ ２６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
AbdelHadi Ramahi　Eman Abouhassira　Nayera Abdallah

[アル・ジュダイダ（ヨルダン）／ドバイ／カイロ ２６日 ロイター] - ヨルダンは２６日、国内で先週起きた教会襲撃事件の容疑者らがシリア南部で活動する「テロ組織」とつながっていたと判断し、同地域の武装勢力の潜伏先とする場所を空軍が攻撃したと発表した。

ヨルダン軍は、作戦はシリア政府と調整して実施したと説明した。一方、シリア政府はこれと食い違う説明をし、ヨルダンによる攻撃について調査を開始したと明らかにした。声明で、国境地域における現場レベルおよび治安面での調整の重要性を強調した。

シリア外務省は声明で、事前調整のない攻撃に対する「全面的な異議」をヨルダンに伝えたとした。

シリアの保健当局者は国営通信に対し、ヨルダンの攻撃で女性や子どもを含む民間人５人が死亡したと述べた。これについて、ヨルダンから直ちにコメントは得られなかった。

これに先立ち、ヨルダンの治安当局者は２６日、９人が死亡した教会襲撃事件に関与した疑いで、銃撃戦の末に兄弟２人と義理の兄弟１人を逮捕したと明らかにしていた。容疑者らと他の組織とのつながりはないとみられ、独自に行動したとの見方を示していた。

中東で比較的安定しているヨルダンでは、こうした暴力事件は極めて異例。少数派のキリスト教徒を狙った２３日の襲撃を受け、アブドラ国王は「断固たる措置」を取るよう治安部隊に命じた。 

この事件は２３日、首都アンマンの南西約１２０キロにあるカラク県ハムード村のギリシャ正教会で葬儀中に発生し、少なくとも３４人が負傷した。目撃者によると、銃撃は数分間続いたという。 

公安当局はカラクの廃屋に潜伏していた容疑者を発見したと説明。投降を拒否して治安部隊を攻撃したため、部隊が応戦し、３人全員を負傷させた上で逮捕した。

治安部隊側に負傷者はでなかった。容疑者らが所持していた複数の銃器や弾薬が見つかったという。

items.title: Netanyahu touts Trump endorsement on eve of vote, suggests they may restart war on Iran
items.author: Steven Scheer, Emily Rose
items.creator: Steven Scheer, Emily Rose
items.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu boasted of his endorsement from Donald Trump on the eve of Israel's election, suggesting the two leaders could restart their war against Iran if he wins.
items.body:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu boasted of his endorsement from Donald Trump on the eve of Israel's election, suggesting the two leaders could restart their war against Iran if he wins, after Trump said they should "finish the job".
"US President Donald Trump has come with a friendship that has never existed before between an Israeli prime minister and an American president. And it is doubtful we will ever have such a friendly president again," Netanyahu said in a televised appearance late on Sunday night. "He has another two years, and he says he is calling on you to vote for me."
In his own social media post on Sunday, Trump, who launched the Iran war jointly with Netanyahu in February, said: "Vote for Bibi Netanyahu for Prime Minister, we have to finish the job that we started!"
Netanyahu said Trump was willing to take action "that would finally, finally, remove the Iranian threat", but only as long as Netanyahu himself remains in power.
"And I have already instructed the Mossad and the IDF (military) to bring down this regime, to bring down this regime because that is the only way to put an end to this threat," Netanyahu said, referring to Israel's main intelligence service and military.
Asked for comment on Netanyahu's remarks, White House Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly said: “As President Trump stated, Iran is in very bad condition, both economically and militarily, and the blockade will remain in full force and effect, with oil flowing in record numbers of barrels through the Hormuz Strait."
"The United States will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"]," Kelly added via email, referring to the November 3 vote in the US.
Trump first endorsed Netanyahu on October 18, reiterating his support in a post on Truth Social on Sunday.
Asked by reporters later on Monday whether Netanyahu had requested the second endorsement, Trump said: "I never spoke about it."
"I put out both endorsements. I put out both... I think he's done a very good job as prime minister under very trying conditions."
Netanyahu's leading opponent, centrist former military Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, posted his own comments on social media, praising Trump as "a true friend of Israel".
"I value his efforts and his commitment to Israel’s security, and I am confident that he will work in full cooperation with any leader chosen by the people."
EISENKOT ACCUSES NETANYAHU OF FEAR-MONGERING Tuesday's vote, Israel's first since the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks, is the first chance for voters to deliver a [USN:L8N4680E4 TEXT:"verdict on the worst security failure"] in generations and the wars on multiple fronts that followed.
With Netanyahu already at the helm of the most right-wing government in Israeli history, politics have shifted even further to the right. Nearly all Jewish-led parties, including that of the hawkish Eisenkot, now [USN:L6N4660BW TEXT:"oppose the "two-state solution" that underpinned decades of peace negotiations"] with the Palestinians.
But many voters say the divisive politics of Israel's longest-serving leader make the country weaker. Polls suggest Netanyahu's Likud Party will lose seats, potentially depriving his coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties of its narrow majority.
Eisenkot and an array of opposition parties ranging from the rump of the centre-left to the right, also have no clear path to unseat him.
Netanyahu, 77, is an unrivaled master of political survival: the only time since 2009 that opponents managed to wrest him briefly from the premiership, it took four inconclusive elections within two years to get him out. He was back 18 months later.
Neither side planned major public events for Monday. But both posted on social media, drumming on the election's major themes — for Netanyahu, that he is the only leader with the mettle to face down Israel's enemies; for his opponents, that his divisive politics have weakened the country.
Netanyahu shared an AI-generated video on Monday of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, whose father Ali Khamenei was killed on the first night of US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. Lying in a hospital bed, the younger Khamenei says his own vote would be "definitely not Bibi. Another term like this and I will be meeting my father sooner than expected."
On Sunday Netanyahu posted a computer-generated photo of a mushroom cloud over Tel Aviv, saying Israel was in existential danger from Iran.
[USN:L6N46303T TEXT:"Eisenkot responded"] by accusing him of "relying on a campaign of fear-mongering, lies, and threats—including images of nuclear bombs in the heart of Tel Aviv. This time, it won’t work for him."
Trump's endorsement of Netanyahu carries its own political risks a week before a legislative election in which his own Republicans are seeking to hold onto power.
The Iran war is deeply unpopular in the United States, blamed for a surge in prices especially for fuel. Major fighting has been suspended for months after ceasefire negotiations held without Israeli participation.

items.title: Anthropic's soaring sales, steep losses put AI frenzy to IPO test
items.author: Manya Saini, Echo Wang
items.creator: Manya Saini, Echo Wang
items.summary: Anthropic took a big step closer to a potentially record-breaking IPO on Monday, even as it revealed steep losses and security concerns that could test investors' enthusiasm for the AI heavyweight.
items.body:
Anthropic took a big step closer to a potentially record-breaking IPO on Monday, even as it revealed steep losses and security concerns that could test investors' enthusiasm for the AI heavyweight.
AI has captured investors' imagination with the promise of a technological leap that could transform businesses, accelerate scientific breakthroughs and unlock vast productivity gains.
That has fueled enormous investments in computing infrastructure and AI development, while also stoking skepticism over the scale and pace of the spending.
Anthropic's listing comes at a critical time for global markets as investors closely assess whether the billions of dollars being poured into the technology will generate returns to justify sky-high valuations.
"There is still enormous excitement about AI's potential to transform businesses, turbocharge productivity and reshape entire industries, but investors are becoming more discerning," said Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.
Anthropic's net loss in the first half of 2026 [USN:L4N4661JI TEXT:"widened sharply"] to $80.7 billion, largely due to a non-operating item related to bonds convertible into the company's shares.
Despite the huge expenses, its operating loss for the same period narrowed to $693 million and its adjusted operating income swung to a positive $1.62 billion compared with a loss of $1.85 billion a year ago.
The company, which is expected to go public before Thanksgiving, said its revenue grew a staggering 1,368% in the three months ended June 30 from a year ago, but it warned in the prospectus that its revenue growth rate could decline and fluctuate from time to time.
The filing [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"confirmed a series of Reuters "][USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"exclusives"] that offered an early peek at its contents before Anthropic made it public, including details of its financial performance, growth trajectory and IPO plans.
Its prospectus details the risks from the powerful technology, from potential misuse and security threats to concerns that advanced systems could produce outputs that "could be interpreted as coercive, deceptive, or manipulative", including behavior resembling blackmail.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei [USN:L1N45403P TEXT:"has called for a slowdown"] in the development of AI.
VALUATION EXPECTATIONS Some current and prospective investors [USN:L6N4611F6 TEXT:"are valuing Anthropic"] at about $1.5 trillion, down from roughly $2 trillion a week ago, after the AI startup disclosed some financial details at a [USN:L6N4601DE TEXT:"recent investor event"].
"The offering is for the faithful, that sooner or later, they're going to get some return on that invested capital," said Thomas Hayes, chairman at Great Hill Capital.
Anthropic's IPO [USN:L6N46216E TEXT:"currently stands alone"] in what was once expected to be a crowded fall listing market. Analysts [USN:L6N46C0UF TEXT:"said"] that would give it access to a deep pool of capital to fund its costly AI ambitions.
"Anthropic's IPO will establish a benchmark for valuing leading AI labs, influencing both upcoming listings and confidence in the companies funding the AI infrastructure build-out," IPOX research associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.
Analysts expect valuations of the AI sector to correct as [USN:L6N4611C1 TEXT:"investor unease"] with the debt-fueled AI investment boom roils equity and debt markets. Higher borrowing costs and rising bond yields have also added to investor caution.
"Anthropic is entering an IPO market that is far more challenging than the summer. Investors were not questioning valuations the same way a few months ago," said Matt Kennedy, senior strategist at Renaissance Capital, a provider of IPO-focused research and ETFs.
BALANCING AI'S PROMISES AND PERILS Anthropic said more than half of Fortune 500 companies and over 30% of Global 2000 firms were its customers that generated at least $100,000 each in revenue for the company over the 12 months ended September 30.
The IPO comes as Anthropic's own research raises concerns about advanced AI systems, which in controlled tests have shown behaviors including code sabotage, fraud assistance and information manipulation.
"Our increasing use of AI systems to accelerate our own research and development may cause the capabilities of our models to advance more rapidly than our ability to develop, validate, and implement corresponding safety, alignment, and security measures," the prospectus said.
The company said it relies on a limited number of cloud services providers such as Amazon, Google and Microsoft and suppliers such as Broadcom for compute and critical infrastructure parts. These relationships can create "dependencies and potential vulnerabilities", it said.
Anthropic, which [USN:L4N41X0QE TEXT:"did not reveal"] the terms of its offering, will trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT" after the [USN:L4N469189 TEXT:"IPO closes"].
SCORCHING PACE OF GROWTH Anthropic, founded in 2021 by a team of researchers who left OpenAI after disagreements over governance and AI safety, was [USN:L4N4251UW TEXT:"valued at $965 billion"] in a funding round in May. It remains locked in a fierce battle with OpenAI to lead the race to build the most advanced AI systems.
The company named Netflix's billionaire co-founder Reed Hastings as its lead independent director. In keeping with Nasdaq rules, Anthropic identified itself as a "controlled company" based on the power of its Long-Term Benefit Trust to elect a majority of its board.
The company said it expects compute and infrastructure expenses to rise in absolute dollars and remain its largest operating expense.
Anthropic has committed more than $600 billion to computing deals with partners including Amazon and Google, ranking among the largest AI infrastructure commitments on record.
Anthropic's IPO follows that of Elon Musk's SpaceX, which rewrote the IPO record books in June, when it [USN:L6N42G18Z TEXT:"priced"] a $75 billion offering that valued the company at $1.75 trillion.
Goldman Sachs secured the prestigious lead-left role on Anthropic's IPO, working alongside Morgan Stanley, which is also a lead underwriter. Both banks declined to comment.
Twenty other banks were named as underwriters with Morgan Stanley serving as stabilization agent, overseeing the stock's early trading. The IPO mandates mark another win for the two banks, which also held lead roles in SpaceX's IPO.

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 26 : Cadence Design Systems on Monday launched a portfolio of AI models tuned to help design computer chips, deepening its open-source model work with Nvidia and diverging from rival Synopsys' recent deal with OpenAI.
Both companies make software used to design computing chips — a process that involves arranging billions of transistors precisely to meet cost and performance targets — and are racing to have AI "agents" use those tools on behalf of human engineers to speed up the process.
The new suite, called Cadence Maestro, introduced on Monday, was built in part on Nvidia's open-weight Nemotron model and secured with Nvidia's OpenShell safety technology, the companies said.
Cadence said customers can run the models on its own cloud or any public cloud, or keep them entirely in-house behind their own firewalls and data centers.

Shares of Cadence, which reports earnings after market close on Monday, rose 3.9 per cent after the announcement.
Customers can also fine-tune the models on their own chip designs, and early results show up to 30 per cent higher quality and up to five times better cost-efficiency than general-purpose models, it added.
The Cadence approach contrasts with that of its largest competitor, Synopsys, which on September 30 said it would develop an AI model with OpenAI and share revenue with the ChatGPT maker. That model, GPT-Synopsys, will run on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure.
Paul Cunningham, a Cadence senior vice president, framed Maestro as model-agnostic, saying, "there are more (AI) model providers out there than there are (chip design software) vendors."
When asked whether Cadence might strike its own deals with proprietary AI labs, Cunningham said both open- and closed-weight approaches were being "pursued equally," and that working with commercial labs was "part of the Maestro vision," though he declined to elaborate.
The first Maestro models will reach select early-access customers in the fourth quarter, Cadence said.

Oct 26 : T-Mobile on Monday unveiled wireless plans that let customers pick and swap perks from Netflix to DoorDash, moving away from its traditional strategy of locking benefits into fixed plan tiers. 
The move mirrors customizable offerings from rivals such as Verizon, but T-Mobile's new plans include selected streaming, music and other subscriptions at no extra cost beyond the monthly plan price. 
• T-Mobile is betting that offering greater control over benefits will attract customers spending on multiple subscriptions, as competition among US carriers moves beyond network coverage and smartphone promotions
• Netflix was the most popular benefit in a pilot launched in early October, T-Mobile Chief Marketing Officer Allan Samson told Reuters in an interview

AI skittishness has put the brakes on Wall Street's rally, resuscitating [USN:L4N46803Y TEXT:"demand for US Treasuries"] as investors seek to protect portfolios, even as surging energy prices stoke inflation. This could put the Federal Reserve in an unenviable stagflationary bind.
For most of this year, the US bond market has been slammed by an inflation-inducing barrage of soaring energy prices, fiscal fears, and the AI boom. Two of those forces remain very much in play, yet bond yields are no longer on a one-way path higher, with the 10-year falling below 5% for the first time in over a month last Thursday.
Investor sentiment around AI is souring. While there has been no single obvious trigger, long-held concerns about the vast sums being spent on the technology have been exacerbated by Big Tech earnings reports detailing gargantuan capital expenditure plans. AI debt markets are wobbling too. While this all may prove to be temporary – just another speed bump in the AI race – the mood shift suggests we may be at the point in the cycle where almost any news is bad news.
If so, this should spur a rally in “risk-free” Treasuries. If the AI juggernaut is sputtering, Wall Street and Main Street should sputter too, given how fundamental the technology has become to the stock market and economic growth.
But the alarming fiscal outlook hasn't changed, and energy prices are roaring higher again, with US crude futures rising 10% last week to a six-month peak above $110 a barrel, suggesting price pressures and inflation expectations aren't cooling anytime soon.
PERSISTENT PRICE PRESSURES A glance at a chart of the 10-year Treasury yield shows how closely correlated energy prices and the bond market have been this year. The 10-year yield's lowest daily close in 2026 was 3.96% on Friday, February 27, the day before the US and Israel attacked Iran. The subsequent surge in global crude, gas and fuel prices then propelled Treasury yields to their highest levels in more than two decades as investors bet that inflationary pressures would intensify. The 10-year yield reached 5.36% earlier this month.
But that relationship has broken down recently. Oil prices eased for a few weeks beginning in mid-September, but the relentless rise in bond yields continued. Now oil prices have rebounded sharply, yet Treasury yields are in retreat, culminating in last Thursday's steep decline of 20 basis points.
Typically, a global energy shock would be expected to slow economic growth, causing investors to flee to the Treasury market. However, for most of this year, the tailwind from the AI juggernaut has kept the economy and Wall Street humming.
If the AI narrative is turning, bond investors will have to consider the potential valuation destruction and economic fallout from a deflating AI bubble. That appears to be offsetting any fears of "higher-for-longer" energy prices. But the move back toward Treasuries may not be a simple switch to flick.
'STAGFLATION' RETURN? That’s because "stagflation" could return to investors' lexicon.
A mix of stagnant growth and sticky inflation would complicate life for the Federal Open Market Committee. While it raised its policy rate in September, it will almost certainly keep it on hold this Wednesday ahead of next week's midterm elections. Markets still expect it to tighten again in the coming months, but that assumes inflationary pressures outweigh AI wobbles.
Last week, one-year market-based inflation expectations climbed to 2.80%, as measured by inflation swaps. That’s the highest since June, though the rise in longer-dated inflation swap rates has been less dramatic, suggesting investors don't believe the energy shock will become deeply embedded in higher goods and services prices.
Fed policymakers will likely be banking on that. But it's a risky bet.
Producer prices, often a leading indicator of consumer prices, are rising at the fastest pace in four years. The gap between producer and consumer price inflation is also the widest in four years. And it's worth repeating that consumer price inflation has been above the Fed's 2% target for close to six years.
"All main inflation measures are expected to increase over the next couple of months as base effects from last year's government shutdown in October and November create a low bar for rising inflation," UBS economists say. "We expect little easing in inflation before the spring of next year," when the base effects from the start of the Iran war kick in.
Can the Fed afford to "look through" the latest spike in energy prices, while hoping that the AI wobbles don't snowball?
(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters)

BRUSSELS, Oct 26 : The European Commission said on Monday it had accepted Chinese online retail platform Temu's action plan to remedy a breach of the EU's Digital Services Act, following a fine imposed on the company in May.
The plan focuses on five measures to remedy the breach, and Temu now has four months to conduct an interim risk assessment, the Commission, which acts as EU regulator, said in a statement.
The Commission had imposed a €200 million ($224.08 million) fine on Temu in May for not doing enough to stop the sale of illegal products.
A spokesperson for Temu, which is owned by PDD Holdings, said it welcomed the Commission's approval of its plan under which the company will have to assess possible shortcomings of its content moderation system, among other steps.
Temu, along with Shein and other ecommerce platforms, has been hit by the EU imposing €3 fees on low-value ecommerce packages since the start of July. Parcels worth less than €150 previously entered the bloc duty-free.

items.title: CAE to sell airline operations software business Flightscape to SITA in $500 million deal
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Canada's CAE on Monday said it will sell Flightscape, its airline operations software business, to fellow global aviation technology firm SITA in a deal valued at $500 million, including debt.
items.body:
Canada's CAE (CAE.TO) on Monday said it will sell Flightscape, its airline operations software business, to fellow global aviation technology firm SITA in a deal valued at $500 million, including debt.
The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027.
Flightscape helps airlines plan flights, manage crews and coordinate ground and in-flight services
The Flightscape deal comes five months after CAE first said it would pursue a [USN:L4N41O10J TEXT:"strategic review"] for that business
CAE has stepped up efforts to lower costs and improve cash flow under CEO Matthew Bromberg, including an April job cut that impacted 280 workers
The deal allows CAE to reshape its business around its core civil and defense operations
CAE said it will put the proceeds from the Flightscape sale toward its core simulation and training businesses

items.title: Serbia's new leaders face host of tough challenges
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Serbia's student-led protest movement won a historic victory in Sunday's parliamentary election, ending the long rule of Aleksandar Vucic and sparking mass celebrations. But their yet-to-be named leaders face a long list of issues.
items.body:
Serbia's student-led protest movement [USN:L6N46B017 TEXT:"won a historic victory"] in Sunday's parliamentary election, ending the long rule of Aleksandar Vucic and sparking mass celebrations. But their yet-to-be named [USN:L8N4650K6 TEXT:"leaders"] face a long list of issues.
Here are a few of them:
KOSOVO The Student List believes that Kosovo, which declared independence from Belgrade in 2008, remains an integral part of Serbia. During their campaign, the students' candidates said that Kosovo is a temporarily occupied territory which could be reintegrated into Serbia through peaceful means, diplomacy and dialogue.
Their focus is preventing the exodus of the Serbian population in the north of Kosovo, and strengthening institutions funded by Serbia and operating under the Serbian legal system, such as healthcare and education. They want Kosovo's Serb communities to operate autonomously, rejecting previous agreements with the ethnic Albanian-led government in Pristina, such as those on energy, vehicle licence plates and the use of the dinar currency.
FRAYED EU RELATIONS With Serbia's European Union accession talks largely stalled by a lack of necessary reforms, the Student List campaign deliberately avoided such polarising foreign policy issues.
Prominent candidates, including former central bank governor Dejan Soskic and cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, have said the government must first focus on domestic reforms and close all EU negotiating clusters before asking the public to cast a definitive ballot on membership of the bloc.
The Student List position on Kosovo is also at odds with membership of the EU, which requires Belgrade to normalise relations with Pristina.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the bloc [USN:L6N46B0AC TEXT:"stood ready to support reforms"] including on the rule of law and media freedom, and to work together to advance Serbia’s future in the EU.
COMPLEX RUSSIAN RELATIONSHIP AND US SANCTIONS AGAINST NIS OIL FIRM The Student List must navigate an intricate energy and foreign policy web with traditional Serbian ally Russia. The students have said they have no plans to align with the EU and impose sanctions on Moscow over its war in Ukraine.
The new government would be reliant on US sanctions waivers to maintain crude imports while it waits for the [USN:L1N45M0TB TEXT:"sale of Russia's stake"] in energy company NIS (NIIS.BEL) , which operates Serbia's only oil refinery, to Hungary’s MOL (MOLB.BU) .
Russia's Gazprom (GAZP.MM) is also Serbia’s biggest gas supplier, delivering around 2.2 billion cubic meters a year at below-market pricing. The Student List said this energy reliance was not a geopolitical alignment, but an acute economic dependency.
The Student List's top candidates had not said whether a future government would end all arms exports from Serbia to war zones, including sales to Western intermediaries who pass weapons to Ukraine. Vucic cultivated strong personal ties with both Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
CORRUPTION The Student List’s anti-corruption program centres on institutional overhauls, such as the creation of an independent police unit accountable to prosecutors rather than the Interior Ministry and a purge of police officers linked to organised crime or violent crackdowns on protests.
They want a ban on the appointments of party loyalists to state-owned companies in favour of transparent, merit-based hiring. Financial accountability and fiscal oversight would include a strict asset origin law allowing the state to audit, seize and return illegally acquired wealth from officials to the state budget.
Convicted officials would be barred from holding public office. The students' anti-corruption program also envisions public scrutiny of all major state infrastructure contracts and the creation of independent oversight bodies to curb the misuse of public funds.
Vucic, the SNS and the authorities repeatedly denied accusations of repression and corruption.
ECONOMY Serbia's economy is deeply integrated with both the European market and international investment flows.
The IMF has forecast Serbia's economic growth at 3% in 2026 and 4% in 2027. Inflation in September stood at 4.1%, almost double August's 2.2%, while the central bank has maintained a 5.75% benchmark rate since 2024.
The Student List’s economic platform shifts Serbia’s growth model away from state-backed infrastructure projects and cheap labour to domestic market security and labour rights.
Central to the plan is a campaign against retail monopolies to lower food prices, coupled with a tax overhaul that raises levies on wealthy citizens and cuts them for lower-income groups.
The movement has pledged to sharply lower the maximum allowed duration for temporary work.
Fiscal sustainability would rely heavily on anti-corruption savings and rigorous state oversight. Social spending would be focused on curbing a youth exodus through an affordable housing initiative for young couples, teachers and healthcare staff, alongside guaranteeing free school textbooks and cheaper, state-subsidised medication.

Oct 26 : SpaceX said on Monday an affiliate of Apollo Global Management will buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the rockets-to-AI firm, in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion.
Each lease will run a little over five years from the day the equipment arrives, according to a regulatory filing.
The deal highlights SpaceX's heavy spending, as it tries to capitalize on surging demand for computing power to help bankroll its Moon and Mars ambitions.
The company aims to finalize the deal by the end of the year. The leases are expected to start in the first half of 2027, once the chips are delivered.

Oct 26 : Shares of neocloud companies declined on Monday after SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the sector could face consolidation and failures, adding to concerns over a widening gap between AI infrastructure investment and revenue generation.
CoreWeave, which has become a poster child for mounting concerns over heavy AI spending, declined 1.6 per cent, while Nebius Group fell 4 per cent and IREN lost 1.5 per cent.
Shares of Applied Digital shed 2 per cent.
In a social media post on Sunday, Musk said that neocloud companies would face significant consolidation and failures, adding that SpaceX would not buy any neocloud companies, calling it "pointless".

"200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many," he said.
"Musk is correct. You're going to need another source of revenue and profits in order to finance these projects moving forward. The cost of capital is too high to make the returns attractive," said Thomas Hayes, chairman at Great Hill Capital in New York.
In an email to Reuters, a CoreWeave spokesperson said that the company continues to see opportunities to finance its growth, underscored by qualities such as "differentiated technology".
Musk was not alone in flagging the risks to the sector.
Earlier this month, research firm Gartner said CoreWeave was at the top of the 100-odd neoclouds most exposed to the increasing leverage, and added that 80 per cent of the companies could cease independent operations by 2032.
Some brokerages expect AI spending to shoot past a trillion dollars next year, adding to investor concerns about the repercussions of severe dependence on debt, at a time when AI assets face rapid depreciation and markets price in more interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.
Bonds of Nebius maturing in 2034 and those of CoreWeave expiring in 2033 have hit record lows on the concerns.
CoreWeave, Nebius, Applied Digital and TeraWulf have reported quarterly losses over the past one year, while IREN has not turned a profit in the past three quarters, raising scrutiny over profitability.
Shares of CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN have fallen more than 30 per cent this month alone. Investors betting on their fall have raked in at least $6 billion in paper profits.

items.author: Ng Hong Siang

CNA Explains: Why are the Houthis targeting Saudi airports?

Saudi Arabia's main international airport in Riyadh has been a repeated target of attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels. CNA looks at why the Houthis are repeatedly targeting Saudi civilian infrastructure, and what this means for travel in the Middle East.

FAST

Saudi Arabia's main international airport in Riyadh has become a repeated target of attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels, disrupting flights and raising concerns about the security of civilian aviation in the kingdom.
On Monday (Oct 26), the Saudi-led military coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis towards Riyadh, after the Iran-backed group claimed another attack on King Khalid International Airport.
The latest incident came as flights resumed at the airport following weeks of disruption, with the Houthis warning airlines and travellers that the facility remained "unsafe" and a "military target".
But the Houthis' attacks on Saudi airports are not new. As far back as November 2017, the group fired a ballistic missile towards King Khalid International Airport, which Saudi authorities said they intercepted.

In June 2019, a missile struck Abha International Airport in southern Saudi Arabia, injuring 26 civilians.
The latest escalation has been particularly deadly. Earlier this month, an attack on Riyadh airport killed 13 people and wounded more than 300 , marking the deadliest such incident in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.
The attacks have disrupted travel plans for thousands of passengers, forced the postponement of Saudi Arabia's flagship investment conference until 2027 and cast uncertainty over the kingdom's ambitions to become a global tourism and business hub .
CNA looks at why the Houthis are repeatedly targeting Saudi civilian infrastructure, and what this means for travel in the Middle East.

Houthi activists stand on a platform against a banner depicting Houthi missiles at an anti-Saudi rally amid an escalation with the kingdom, in Sanaa, Yemen on Jul 31, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Khaled Abdullah)

Why are the Houthis targeting airports? Airports are among a country's most strategically and economically important infrastructure, making them particularly disruptive targets during a conflict.
The Houthis' raids on Saudi airports are part of a wider series of attacks on the kingdom's infrastructure, including on oil tankers and pumping stations.
Missiles have also been fired towards the Saudi cities of Taif and Yanbu. The latter is a major oil export hub on the Red Sea coast that has allowed Riyadh to bypass Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
The Houthis have described Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport as a military target and warned airlines against using it.
However, the group's claims do not by themselves establish that the airport is a lawful military target under international humanitarian law.
United Nations secretary-general António Guterres has called for an immediate halt to attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, saying that they violate international law. 
Besides Riyadh, airports in Abha, Dammam, Najran and Jizan have also come under attack.
The Houthis' targeting of critical infrastructure bears similarities to tactics used by their main backer, Iran, which has also launched attacks on infrastructure across Gulf Arab states.

Related:

Flights resume at Riyadh airport as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia

CNA Explains: How the Houthis could threaten the Red Sea and shape the Iran war

What triggered the latest escalation? The conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis dates back to 2015, when Riyadh led a military intervention in Yemen against the Iran-backed group.
A United Nations-brokered truce in April 2022 brought a significant reduction in hostilities, including cross-border attacks. Although the ceasefire formally expired six months later, a relative calm largely held.
Tensions flared again in July 2026 when the Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of launching airstrikes on Sanaa International Airport in Yemen's capital.
Yemen's internationally recognised government's defence ministry said the strikes were intended to prevent an Iranian aircraft from landing at the airport.
The Houthis subsequently launched missile and drone attacks on Abha International Airport, with no casualties reported.
The group also declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began targeting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before launching a major offensive in September in which they seized Yemeni government-held territory along the Red Sea coast.
The Houthis have also reported frequent Saudi airstrikes on areas under their control.

What impact are these attacks having on Saudi Arabia? The Houthi attacks have severely disrupted Saudi Arabia's aviation sector, forcing Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport to close for two weeks before resuming operations on Sunday (Oct 25).
The fallout has extended beyond aviation, with several major international events cancelled, postponed or relocated over security concerns.
Saudi Arabia has postponed its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference until 2027, while organisers of the prestigious motor sport race Dakar Rally on Sunday said it would move to a different location. 
Golf's Asian Tour postponed the Saudi International indefinitely and cycling's Urban World Championships was cancelled earlier this month, while the tennis tournament Six Kings Slam was postponed to December.
These disruptions come as Saudi Arabia pursues its Vision 2030 plan to diversify its economy. 
Prolonged instability could undermine investor confidence and make it harder for it to attract international visitors, businesses and major events.
The country's energy infrastructure has also come under threat.
In September, Saudi Arabia temporarily shut down its 1,200km East-West pipeline as a precaution after a drone attack that Riyadh and Baghdad said originated in Iraq. The pipeline has served as a key route for Middle East oil exports amid the war-related disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
On Oct 24, the Houthis claimed to have targeted the pipeline, crude oil pumping stations, an Aramco facility in Yanbu and the Rabigh refinery. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed those claims.

Related:

US orders diplomats to depart Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes

Saudi says intercepted Houthi missile, blasts heard in capital

What is the official advice about travelling to Saudi Arabia? Amid the escalating violence, the United States has ordered some diplomats and their family members to leave its missions in Saudi Arabia , and plans to withdraw family members from several other US missions in the region.
Washington had returned some diplomatic personnel to the region in recent months, after many were pulled out following Iranian attacks on US facilities when the US-Israeli war against Iran began in late February.
On Singapore's part, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has advised Singaporeans to defer all travel to Saudi Arabia , citing an increase in missile and drone attacks targeting civilian aviation and energy infrastructure.
The Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS) has also advised Singaporeans planning to perform Umrah to consider postponing their trips to Saudi Arabia .
Umrah is a voluntary pilgrimage to Mecca that Muslims can undertake at any time of the year.
Despite the advisories, some Singaporeans are pressing ahead with their pilgrimage plans.
Some families CNA spoke to earlier this month said that they were adopting adopt a " wait-and-see” approach, while others have had their pilgrimage cancelled.

Related:

Some Singapore pilgrims press ahead with Umrah plans despite advisory, others face cancellations

Singaporeans advised to defer all travel to Saudi Arabia amid heightened security risks: MFA

Singapore condemns Houthi attacks on civilian aviation infrastructure in Saudi Arabia

Why are the Houthis able to strike Riyadh so often? Iran has provided the Houthis with weapons, funding and training for more than a decade, although Tehran denies arming the group in violation of a United Nations arms embargo.
Despite Iran facing its own financial and military strains due to war and sanctions, the Houthis have learned - with Iranian help - how to assemble their own weapons, including drones and missiles, experts interviewed by Reuters said.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards and members of Iran's other ally, Lebanese Hezbollah, initially gave the Houthis knowledge of missile systems and their operation, Andreas Krieg, senior security studies lecturer at King's College London told Reuters.
"Former Yemeni military engineers and a growing generation of locally trained specialists have helped institutionalise these capabilities," he said.
"Tehran has not simply supplied the Houthis with weapons. It has helped create an indigenous military-industrial learning process that becomes progressively harder to dismantle, even if direct Iranian supply routes are disrupted."
This has made the Houthis one of Iran's most cost-effective and valuable regional military allies.
The group has also reportedly turned to artificial intelligence to enhance its weapons capabilities.
Anthropic said last month that "a cell of threat actors based in northern Yemen" had used its Claude AI assistant to help develop software for a guided rocket, a planned ballistic missile with a range of more than 2,000km and a missile variant incorporating a hypersonic glide vehicle.
Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia's air defences face mounting pressure from repeated missile and drone attacks, even as its US ally grapples with demands on its own air defence resources amid the war with Iran.

Source: CNA/Agencies/nh

items.title: La Jordanie dit avoir frappé des repaires de combattants en Syrie après l'attaque contre une église
items.author: Abdelhadi Ramahi, Yomna Ehab
items.creator: Abdelhadi Ramahi, Yomna Ehab
items.summary: La Jordanie a déclaré lundi que ses forces aériennes ont frappé des repaires de combattants dans le sud de la Syrie en réponse à l'attaque meurtrière de vendredi contre une église dans le sud du pays.
items.body:
La Jordanie a déclaré lundi que ses forces aériennes ont frappé des repaires de combattants dans le sud de la Syrie en réponse à l'attaque meurtrière de vendredi contre une [USN:L6N4690ZM TEXT:"église"] dans le sud du pays.
Les forces de sécurité jordaniennes ont précisé que l'opération avait été menée en coordination avec Damas, ce que le régime syrien dément.
Les autorités syriennes ont dit avoir ouvert une enquête sur les forces jordaniennes, soulignant l'importance de renforcer la coordination de la sécurité dans les régions frontalières.
Damas a fait part de ses "réserves totales" au sujet de frappes qui ont été menées sans coordination préalable, a indiqué le ministère syrien des Affaires étrangères dans un communiqué.
Les frappes jordaniennes ont fait cinq morts civils, dont des femmes et des enfants, a annoncé un dirigeant sanitaire syrien à une agence de presse étatique.
Amman n'a pas fourni de commentaire sur ces événements.
Plus tôt, les forces de sécurité jordaniennes ont annoncé avoir arrêté trois suspects après l'attaque meurtrière perpétrée vendredi.
Ces trois hommes, deux frères et leur beau-frère, ne semblent avoir aucun lien avec des cellules islamistes identifiées, ont déclaré de hauts responsables de la sécurité gouvernementale.
"Si Dieu le veut, ils ne représentent qu'eux-mêmes", a déclaré le directeur de la sécurité publique jordanienne, le major-général Obeidallah al Maaytah, au cours d'une conférence de presse aux côtés du ministre de l'Intérieur Mazen al Faraya.
"Le dossier n'est pas encore clos; les investigations se poursuivent. A ce jour, rien n'indique un lien entre eux et d'autres cellules", a précisé Mazen al Faraya.
Le ministre de l'Intérieur a ajouté que les autorités examinaient les circonstances qui avaient poussé ces assaillants présumés vers l'extrémisme et qu'ils seraient tenus pour responsables si leur participation était confirmée.
Les trois hommes sont soupçonnés d'avoir participé à une attaque survenue vendredi lors de funérailles dans une église grecque orthodoxe du village de Hamoud, dans le gouvernorat de Karak, situé à environ 120 km au sud-ouest d'Amman. Cette attaque a fait neuf morts et 40 blessés, suscitant la crainte au sein de la communauté chrétienne du pays.
La Direction de la sécurité publique jordanienne a indiqué que les suspects avaient été localisés alors qu'ils se cachaient dans une maison abandonnée à Karak. Ils ont refusé de se rendre et ont attaqué les forces de sécurité, qui ont riposté et interpellé les trois hommes après les avoir blessés, a précisé la Direction dans un communiqué publié dans les médias d'État.
Aucun membre des forces de sécurité n'a été blessé lors de l'interpellation, et plusieurs armes à feu ainsi que des munitions ont été retrouvées en possession des suspects.
Le roi Abdallah II, dont le pays s'est allié aux Etats-Unis dans la lutte contre les groupes islamistes, a ordonné aux forces de sécurité de réagir avec une "main de fer" à cette attaque contre la minorité chrétienne.

items.title: "Retour vers le futur" au Brésil? Flavio Bolsonaro, comme jadis son père, refuse de reconnaître la victoire de Lula
items.author: Oliver Griffin, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
items.creator: Oliver Griffin, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
items.summary: Le candidat de la droite brésilienne Flavio Bolsonaro emboîte le pas à son père, l'ex-président condamné pour tentative de coup d'Etat après la présidentielle perdue de 2022, en refusant de reconnaître sa défaite face au président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, qui a remporté dimanche un quatrième mandat historique.
items.body:
Le candidat de la droite brésilienne Flavio Bolsonaro emboîte le pas à son père, l'ex-président condamné pour tentative de coup d'Etat après la présidentielle perdue de 2022, en refusant de reconnaître sa défaite face au président sortant Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, qui a [USN:L5N46C021 TEXT:"remporté"] dimanche un quatrième mandat historique.
Le sénateur de 45 ans conteste une décision prise dimanche soir par un juge de la Cour suprême nommé par Lula, qui a prolongé le second tour de l'élection présidentielle de deux heures en raison d’irrégularités présumées concernant le transport des électeurs. Le fils de Jair Bolsonaro a déclaré qu’il demanderait l’annulation du résultat.
"Il est impossible de reconnaître les résultats de l’élection, compte tenu des circonstances dans lesquelles les événements se sont déroulés", a-t-il déclaré à des journalistes.
Le président américain Donald Trump, autrefois proche allié du père Bolsonaro, a également fait part de ses doutes sur la validité du scrutin, faisant état d'une élection truquée".
"Je n'ai pas pris parti, mais ça ressemble à une nouvelle élection truquée", a-t-il déclaré, sans fournir de preuves.
Parallèlement, de nombreux dirigeants ont salué la victoire de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, les félicitations affluant de l'Union européenne, du Mexique, de la France, du Canada, de l'Inde et de la Russie.
Les présidents de droite récemment élus en Colombie, au Pérou et au Chili ont également rejoint les rangs des dirigeants reconnaissant les résultats de dimanche, mais l'administration américaine du président Donald Trump, proche de la famille Bolsonaro, est restée silencieuse.
Les investisseurs, stupéfaits par la victoire de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, qui a déjoué les sondages, ont fait [USN:L6N46C0UL TEXT:"plonger la Bourse brésilienne"], le taux de change et la dette publique, alors que les marchés réévaluaient les perspectives budgétaires du pays.
Toutefois, l’ampleur de la défaite, Bolsonaro fils accusant un retard de plus de 4 millions de voix sur Lula, rend peu probable le succès de sa tentative pour faire annuler le scrutin, selon des analystes. Sa requête est également compromise par le fait que son équipe avait elle-même demandé une prolongation des opérations de vote en raison de fortes pluies dans le sud du pays, traditionnellement conservateur.
Moins de 35.000 suffrages, soit environ 0,03% du total, ont été exprimés au cours des deux heures supplémentaires de vote ordonnées par la Cour suprême, selon une analyse des registres électoraux réalisée par Pedro Burgos, professeur à l'Insper.
Le refus du fils l'ancien président de reconnaître sa défaite pourrait néanmoins déclencher une vague de manifestations dans un pays où la confiance dans le système électoral et dans l’indépendance judiciaire a été mise à rude épreuve ces dernières années, estiment les observateurs.
Jair Bolsonaro avait plongé le Brésil dans une profonde crise démocratique après les élections de 2022, lorsque ses partisans avaient pris d’assaut des bâtiments gouvernementaux pour protester contre le résultat. Il a par la suite été [USN:L5N3UY1NR TEXT:"condamné"] à 27 ans de prison. Il est depuis lors détenu à domicile, pour des raisons liées à son état de santé.
INTERDICTION DE QUITTER LE BRÉSIL A la suite d'une visite à son père en prison, Flavio Bolsonaro a déclaré que la police fédérale brésilienne lui avait demandé de remettre ses passeports, ajoutant qu'il avait l'intention de coopérer avec les autorités, niant vouloir fuir le pays.
Flavio Bolsonaro a accusé le juge de la Cour suprême Alexandre de Moraes d'être à l'origine de cette décision, sans apporter de preuves.
La Cour suprême brésilienne et la police fédérale n'ont pas répondu à une demande de commentaire.
"On m'a ordonné, en pleine rue, de remettre mes passeports, et on m'a notifié que j'avais pour interdiction de quitter le pays", a déclaré Flavio Bolsonaro dans une vidéo publiée sur ses réseaux sociaux.
Ce dernier affirme que la décision du juge brésilien fait suite aux commentaires de son frère, Eduardo Bolsonaro, qui avait conseillé au candidat à la présidentielle la semaine dernière dans un podcast de fuir le Brésil s'il venait à perdre contre Lula.
La victoire de Lula a déjoué les sondages, coupant court à une vague conservatrice en Amérique latine. Un résultat surprise qui n'est pas non plus du goût de l’administration du président américain Donald Trump, qui a oeuvré pour le retour du clan Bolsonaro au pouvoir.
Les marchés financiers ont également exprimé leurs inquiétudes. Un fonds négocié en Bourse coté à Tokyo et indexé sur l’indice brésilien Bovespa (1325.T) a plongé de près de 15% lors des échanges asiatiques à l’annonce de la victoire de Lula, tandis que les analystes s’attendaient à ce que le real brésilien s’affaiblisse face au dollar américain.
Lula s'était retrouvé en seconde position face à Flavio Bolsonaro au premier tour, mais il a réussi à mobiliser sa base dans l'entre-deux-tours.
S’exprimant dimanche soir dans un hôtel de São Paulo, il a adopté un ton conciliant.
"Je ne parlerai pas d’unité nationale, car cela ne correspond pas toujours à la réalité de ce pays. Personne n’est obligé d’apprécier le président élu, mais celui-ci a été mis en place pour gouverner au nom de tous", a-t-il souligné.
Pendant la campagne, Lula, qui a 80 ans, a mis en avant son bilan en matière de lutte contre la pauvreté et les inégalités, tout en soulignant les taux historiquement bas du chômage, de l’analphabétisme et de la déforestation.
Son quatrième mandat [USN:L6N46C0YC TEXT:"s'annonce difficile"].
Il devra en effet travailler au côté d’un Congrès tenu par les alliés de Bolsonaro, après une vague conservatrice aux élections législatives.
Le président français Emmanuel Macron a déclaré que la France et le Brésil avaient "beaucoup à construire ensemble", tandis que la présidente de la Commission européenne, Ursula von der Leyen, a affirmé que "la démocratie et le multilatéralisme avaient triomphé au Brésil".
Le Kremlin a salué la réélection de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva et l’a félicité pour sa contribution aux relations bilatérales et au groupe des BRICS.
Le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky a félicité le dirigeant de gauche pour ses "résultats électoraux remarquables" et a déclaré qu’il se réjouissait à l’idée d’approfondir la coopération.

items.title: 楽天トラベル、顧客情報260万件に不正アクセス　クレジットカード情報3.6万件
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [東京 ２６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[東京 ２６日 ロイター] - 楽天グループは２６日、旅行予約サービス「楽天トラベル」の顧客情報最大２６０万件が不正アクセスを受けたと発表した。最大４万件については氏名やメールアドレス電話番号などが、うち最大３万６０００件はクレジットカード情報が不正アクセスを受けた。

クレジットカード情報には、発行者識別番号と下４桁、名義人名、有効期限、国際ブランド区分が含まれる。セキュリティコードは対象外だという。

不正アクセスを受けたのは、海外ホテル予約サイトのうち、シンガポール子会社が管理・運営する一部のページ。９月１０日に異常を検知し、１５日に原因を特定、１６日にシステム改修を完了したとしている。

また、楽天トラベルの多言語予約サイトも１０月２０日に不正アクセスの可能性を検知。最大８６万件の顧客メールアドレスと社内用識別番号が不正アクセスの対象となった。

(Corrects paragraph 8 and graphic to additional (not total) technology spending following clarification from Deutsche Bank)
By Tom Sims and Hakan Ersen
FRANKFURT, Oct 26 : AI is helping Deutsche Bank cut decisions for some smaller corporate lending from weeks to just minutes, its new technology chief Marie-Jeanne Deverdun told Reuters.
The project, which went live in the summer, also reduces the time taken to make some lending decisions for multinational corporations from months to weeks, said Deverdun, who joined Deutsche Bank's management board this year.

"For smaller corporates, which are less complicated in their setup and their legal structure, we're talking weeks to minutes," Deverdun said in an interview.
Deverdun said Deutsche Bank is also preparing for a future when its AI agents will interact directly with clients' own agents, as lenders are drawn into the debate among technology leaders over whether AI development is moving too fast.
"We are watching that debate carefully. These are very valid concerns, and, obviously, the management of cyber risk is my number one priority," she said.
"We're spending a lot of resources and budget to continue to protect the bank from those new technologies and threats," she added.
Banking regulators are stepping up efforts to contain growing AI risk as lenders race to deploy the technology while balancing questions over returns and security threats.
Deutsche Bank plans more than €2.5 billion ($2.80 billion) in additional technology spending between 2026 and 2028. Germany's largest lender does not disclose its total technology spending. JPMorgan is budgeting $20 billion for 2026.
Banks hope AI will trim costs and boost productivity.
Britain's Barclays said last week it was cutting around 5,000 jobs or 5 per cent of its workforce this year as it uses the technology. Citigroup has said AI was now developing products at lower cost and up to 40 per cent faster.
Major US banks, meanwhile, have begun blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside customer accounts in response to concerns that sophisticated AI agents could harm the banking system and the institutions trusted to hold people's wealth.
Deutsche Bank CEO Christian Sewing has said he wants to make Deutsche "a truly AI-powered bank" after his predecessor said in 2015 its systems were "disjointed, cumbersome and far too often just plain incompatible".
After the Ukraine war began, Deutsche Bank had to move its tech staff out of Russia and it is still streamlining an array of platforms, although it has cited some recent progress.
Deverdun said Deutsche Bank had built an internal AI platform known as ADA, named after computing pioneer Ada Lovelace, to develop, monitor and control AI agents.
ADA allows the bank to oversee agent activity, manage risk and switch between AI models as technology evolves, she said.
"We're already preparing for an agentic economy where our agents interact with the agents of our clients with clear accountability and the right controls," she added.
($1 = 0.8937 euros)

items.title: Trend hedge funds saw worst week since 2024 as AI stocks fell, Goldman says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Trend-following hedge funds witnessed their worst weekly performance in two years last week, as concern about the eventual pay-off from hefty AI spending ignited volatility across stocks and bonds, a Goldman Sachs note seen by Reuters on Monday showed.
items.body:
Trend-following hedge funds witnessed their worst weekly performance in two years last week, as concern about the eventual pay-off from hefty AI spending ignited volatility across stocks and bonds, a Goldman Sachs note seen by Reuters on Monday showed.
The Nasdaq 100 (.NDX) , home to the world's largest tech stocks, fell 5.5% last week, its biggest weekly fall since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump's Liberation Day tariffs roiled world markets.
Last week's stock market fall was led in part by a 10% weekly slide in shares of Meta (META.O) , which reported strong earnings, but indicated it would need to raise more capital for its AI investments, which sent shivers through markets.
Bond markets were also volatile, as investors sought out the relative safety of US Treasuries, while selling the debt of more fragile economies, such as France.
Here's what the note said:
Systematic long-short hedge funds, whose algorithms ride market trends until they peter out, suffered their worst week since 2024, with a 2% decline, while fundamental long/short strategies drew down another 1.1%.
Fundamental long short strategies are down 3.8% for the month so far, but still up 8.8% this year, while systematic strategies are down 1.1% so far in October, but up 18.7% so far this year.
Single stocks collectively saw the largest de-gross activity - a general pulling back in positions - since late July, while US equities have been net sold for the third straight week, and in four out of the last five weeks, the note said
Goldman said its prime brokerage desk reported $20 billion in selling of tech stocks over the last two weeks, close to July's major unwind in which saw $23 billion in selling.

items.title: French students vow more protests despite Macron government's concessions
items.author: Makini Brice, Inti Landauro
items.creator: Makini Brice, Inti Landauro
items.summary: French student leaders vowed to go on protesting despite government concessions on education, keeping pressure on President Emmanuel Macron as the movement spreads to unions and other activists, stokes unrest and deepens the economic damage.
items.body:
French student leaders vowed to go on protesting despite government concessions on education, keeping pressure on President Emmanuel Macron as the movement spreads to unions and other activists, stokes unrest and deepens the economic damage.
The measures included a commitment to cap the size of some high school classes; €4 billion ($4.5 billion) of loans for renovating schools; and the replacement by 2028 of a university admissions system students see as socially unfair.
"Not all our demands were met. We'll go on for as long as it takes," Louis Letoublon, one of the representatives of high school students, said as he and fellow student leaders emerged from a meeting with government officials in Paris.
The protests, which have broadened beyond education to draw in trade unions and yellow-vest activists, known for their high-visibility jackets, pose a test for Macron's minority government.
The government has little room to spend its way out of the unrest, with national debt approaching 120% of GDP, while the turmoil is boosting support for far-right frontrunner Marine Le Pen ahead of next year's presidential election.
The package included €1 billion of investment in university campuses; a move to increase student grants with inflation; and the opening up of a further 15,000 higher education places for students.
"It's clear we have to ease the pressure being felt in the education system," Education Minister Edouard Geffray told a press conference.
There was no overall figure for how much funding the package would require. High borrowing needs are already complicating efforts to [USN:L8N4660JK TEXT:"agree"] a budget for next year.
The protests, initially triggered by student discontent, have shown little sign of ending [USN:L1N46608H TEXT:"after violence"] nine days ago engulfed dozens of cities, leading to fears the state had lost control of the streets.
Earlier, Macron acknowledged it was likely there would be more unrest this weekend ahead of a bigger nationwide day of protests set for November 5.
On a tour to survey the damage in Marseille and to thank emergency services after Saturday's protests, he said he would keep security measures in place and work to move protests outside city centres.
[USN:L5N46B05E TEXT:"Candidate"] Le Pen, already the frontrunner in next year's presidential election, has benefited from the unrest and perceptions that authorities are struggling to keep the peace.
An opinion poll published on Sunday put her on 32% to 33.5%, well ahead of her nearest rival, hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon on 17%. Surveys suggest she would easily defeat Melenchon in a run-off ballot, expected to be held in early May.
FAR-RIGHT GANGS CONFRONT FAR-LEFT ACTIVISTS Interior Minister Laurent Nunez earlier said that 1,435 people were arrested nationwide during demonstrations on Saturday and that police had also recorded a new phenomenon, with organised far-right gangs confronting far-left activists in several cities.
"We knew there had been calls from numerous identity-based and nationalist movements to come out, officially, to defend businesses," he said. "In a number of cities, such as Nice and Montpellier, these groups arrived in organised formations, mainly to target the ultra-left movement."
A selloff in French government bonds paused on Monday after rating agency [USN:L1N469154 TEXT:"Moody's"] on Friday refrained from downgrading the country's sovereign debt.
But business leaders said the unrest was continuing to inflict heavy economic damage.
Alain Di Crescenzo, head of the CCI France network of chambers of commerce and industry, said many retailers had remained closed as a precaution after the violence of October 17, adding this had led to sharp falls in sales.
"We have shopkeepers who are tired and demoralised, and we are killing local commerce," he told Radio Classique.

items.title: Barril cae ante esperanzas de paz, ataques a Arabia Saudita limitan las pérdidas
items.author: Siddharth Cavale
items.creator: Siddharth Cavale
items.summary: Los futuros del Brent bajaron el lunes, en medio de las esperanzas de que se suavicen las hostilidades en Oriente Medio, pero los continuos ataques contra Arabia Saudita limitaron las bajas y mantuvieron los precios cerca de sus niveles más altos en seis meses.
items.body:
Los futuros del Brent bajaron el lunes, en medio de las esperanzas de que se suavicen las hostilidades en Oriente Medio, pero los continuos ataques contra Arabia Saudita limitaron las bajas y mantuvieron los precios cerca de sus niveles más altos en seis meses.
* Los futuros del crudo Brent bajaron 91 centavos, o un 0,8%, a 115,81 dólares, mientras que los futuros del West Texas Intermediate (WTI) cayeron 1,51 dólares, o un 1,46%, a 101,76 dólares por barril.
* Ambos referenciales retrocedieron tras las fuertes ganancias registradas el viernes, cuando el Brent cerró con un alza de más de 3 dólares para acumular un incremento semanal del 6%, mientras que el WTI avanzó un 2,3% en la semana.
* La atención de los inversores siguió centrada en la escalada de tensiones en Oriente Medio, después de que los hutíes de Yemen, alineados con Irán, dijeron haber atacado estaciones de bombeo del oleoducto Este-Oeste de Arabia Saudita, así como el aeropuerto de Riad, durante el fin de semana.
* Arabia Saudita informó el domingo que había interceptado más misiles y drones; por su parte, la coalición liderada por los saudíes comunicó el lunes la destrucción de tres drones que tenían como objetivo Riad y las regiones meridionales del reino.
* En una medida que podría involucrar a Egipto de manera más directa en el conflicto, el Parlamento autorizó al presidente Abdel Fattah al-Sisi a adoptar "todas las medidas necesarias" para ayudar a Arabia Saudita a defenderse.
Arabia Saudita, Turquía y Pakistán mantuvieron conversaciones con funcionarios iraníes en Teherán, como parte de los esfuerzos para evitar una mayor escalada en la región. EL encuentro supuso el primer contacto de alto nivel entre Irán y las tres naciones, que firmaron un pacto de defensa mutua en agosto.
Al término, los cuatro países acordaron continuar las conversaciones con el objetivo de reforzar la cooperación en materia de paz y seguridad, informaron los medios estatales iraníes.

items.title: 独ＩＦＯ業況指数、10月90.2で予想以上に改善　先行きを楽観視
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Maria Martinez

[ベルリン ２６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Maria Martinez

[ベルリン ２６日 ロイター] - ドイツのＩＦＯ経済研究所が２６日発表した１０月の業況指数は、先行きへの楽観的な見方が強まったことで、市場予想以上に改善した。改善は６カ月連続。 

業況指数は９０．２と、９月の８９．９から上昇した。ロイターがまとめたアナリスト予想は９０．０だった。

期待指数は９月の９０．４から９１．６に上昇した。

ＩＦＯのクレメンス・フュースト所長は「景気回復は続いている」と述べた。

ＶＰバンクのチーフエコノミスト、トーマス・ギッツェル氏によると、１０月の企業の先行きに対する楽観度は４年半超ぶりの高水準となった。

ドイツ政府は経済成長率予想を引き上げ２０２６年が１．３％、２７年が１．１％とした。４月時点では０．５％、０．９％と予想していた。

ハンブルク商業銀行のチーフエコノミスト、サイラス・デラルビア氏は「ＩＦＯ業況指数が６カ月連続で上昇したことは、数多くの逆風にもかかわらずドイツ経済が成長軌道にあることを示唆している」と述べた。

第３・四半期の成長率は３０日に発表される。

キャピタル・エコノミクスは、ここ数カ月でＩＦＯなど一部の企業調査が改善したものの、第３・四半期はゼロ成長にとどまったと予想している。ただ欧州担当チーフエコノミスト、アンドリュー・ケニンガム氏は「労働市場の回復の兆しや財政刺激策の継続と併せ、今回の調査は第３・四半期の一時的な低迷が一過性の要因にもよるもので、第４・四半期は成長を取り戻すというわれわれの見方を裏付けている」と述べた。

ＶＰバンクのギッツェル氏によると、景況感の改善は全て製造業によるもの。好調な受注と政府のインフラ基金の効果が表れ始め、製造業の景況感を明確に押し上げているという。一方でサービス業は企業の楽観的な見方が後退、家計の消費支出の低迷が原因とみられるという。

ＩＮＧのマクロ調査グローバル責任者、カーステン・ブジェスキ氏は「今回の指数は、ドイツ経済の先行きを巡り継続中の財政刺激策の効果が経済全体に一段と波及することが、引き続き期待されていることを示している」と述べた。

メルツ首相は経済再生に向け、通常予算とは別枠で５０００億ユーロ（５６００億ドル）規模のインフラ基金を創設した。また、軍備増強に向け、憲法に定める借り入れ制限「債務ブレーキ」を見直した。

＜現況判断は悪化＞

期待指数の上昇が業況指数全体を押し上げた一方、現況に対する評価はやや悪化した。現況指数は前月の８９．５から８８．８に低下した。

デラルビア氏は、原油・ガス価格の大幅な上昇が電力価格の上昇や株式市場のボラティリティーにもつながっており、企業に打撃を与えるのは間違いないと指摘。さらに「ドイツ企業にとって２番目に重要な輸出先であるフランス経済が、政治的混乱や債券市場の動揺によってほぼ停滞したままとなれば、その影響はドイツにも及ぶ」との見方を示した。

コメルツ銀行のエコノミスト、イェルク・クレーマー氏は、さまざまなリスクにもかかわらず、ドイツ経済の回復は続く公算が大きいと指摘。ただ「抜本的な改革の欠如、トランプ氏の関税、中国の輸出攻勢により、回復は緩やかなものにとどまるだろう」との見方を示した。

キャピタル・エコノミクスは、ここ数カ月でＩＦＯなど一部の企業調査が改善したものの、第３・四半期はゼロ成長にとどまったと予想している。ただ欧州担当チーフエコノミスト、アンドリュー・ケニンガム氏は「労働市場の回復の兆しや財政刺激策の継続と併せ、今回の調査は第３・四半期の一時的な低迷が一過性の要因にもよるもので、第４・四半期は成長を取り戻すというわれわれの見方を裏付けている」と述べた。

ＶＰバンクのギッツェル氏によると、景況感の改善は全て製造業によるもの。好調な受注と政府のインフラ基金の効果が表れ始め、製造業の景況感を明確に押し上げているという。一方でサービス業は企業の楽観的な見方が後退、家計の消費支出の低迷が原因とみられるという。

ＩＮＧのマクロ調査グローバル責任者、カーステン・ブジェスキ氏は「今回の指数は、ドイツ経済の先行きを巡り継続中の財政刺激策の効果が経済全体に一段と波及することが、引き続き期待されていることを示している」と述べた。

メルツ首相は経済再生に向け、通常予算とは別枠で５０００億ユーロ（５６００億ドル）規模のインフラ基金を創設した。また、軍備増強に向け、憲法に定める借り入れ制限「債務ブレーキ」を見直した。

＜現況判断は悪化＞

期待指数の上昇が業況指数全体を押し上げた一方、現況に対する評価はやや悪化した。現況指数は前月の８９．５から８８．８に低下した。

デラルビア氏は、原油・ガス価格の大幅な上昇が電力価格の上昇や株式市場のボラティリティーにもつながっており、企業に打撃を与えるのは間違いないと指摘。さらに「ドイツ企業にとって２番目に重要な輸出先であるフランス経済が、政治的混乱や債券市場の動揺によってほぼ停滞したままとなれば、その影響はドイツにも及ぶ」との見方を示した。

コメルツ銀行のエコノミスト、イェルク・クレーマー氏は、さまざまなリスクにもかかわらず、ドイツ経済の回復は続く公算が大きいと指摘。ただ「抜本的な改革の欠如、トランプ氏の関税、中国の輸出攻勢により、回復は緩やかなものにとどまるだろう」との見方を示した。

items.title: 米年末商戦の配送料過去最高へ、軽油高騰にサーチャージ算出変更が拍車
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Lisa Baertlein

［ロサンゼルス　２６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Lisa Baertlein

［ロサンゼルス　２６日　ロイター］ - 今年の米国年末商戦の小口貨物配送料金は過去最高となる見通しだ。ディーゼル燃料（軽油）価格の高騰でＵＰＳとフェデックスが燃油サーチャージを引き上げており、米小売業者に逆風が吹いている。しかし、配送コスト上昇は、単純に燃料価格の問題だけではなさそうだ。そこには運送会社のサーチャージ算出方法変更という要因が働いているという。

年末商戦に関連する荷物量は第４・四半期に倍増することもある。大手小売業者を含む荷主１８００社の匿名化データを分析したＴＤコーエン／ＡＦＳ貨物指数によると、同四半期の陸送料金は、ネット通販購入品を含め、前年同期比で５．８％上昇、速達便は１３．８％上昇する見通しだ。同指数は、小口貨物のコストは重量やサイズ、配送先によって異なるため、金額ではなく変化率を示している。

米エネルギー情報局（ＥＩＡ）によると、１０月１９日時点の米国の路上用ディーゼル燃料の平均価格は１ガロン＝６．２８ドルだった。米国とイスラエルが２月２８日にイランを攻撃して以降、６５％上昇したことになる。

ＡＦＳロジスティクスのチーフアナリティクスオフィサー、ミンシュ・ベイツ氏は「燃料は誰にとっても最大の関心事だが、良い材料は見当たらない」と述べた。

＜運送会社の算出方法変更がコスト押し上げ＞

小売業者が頭を痛める輸送コスト。拍車をかけているのは、運送会社の算出方法の変更だ。

ベイツ氏によると、燃油サーチャージコストのうち軽油価格の上昇による分は３０％弱にすぎない。ＵＰＳやフェデックスなど業界大手が算出方法を変更したことにより、サーチャージは燃料価格よりもはるかに速いペースで上昇し、燃料価格が上がらない場合でも上昇しているという。

例えば、２０２１年第１・四半期に軽油価格が２．９１ドルだった時、同指数で燃油サーチャージは基本配送料金の７．７５％だった。仮に軽油価格がこの水準まで下がったとしても、現在の燃油サーチャージは２３．７５％と約３倍になる。燃油サーチャージの算出方法の変更が運送会社の収入を増やし、小売業者のコストを押し上げる構図だ。

各社のサーチャージ表に基づくと、ＥＩＡの平均価格である６．２８ドルでは、ＵＰＳの燃油サーチャージは２９．５％、フェデックスは２９％となる。

ＵＰＳは、料金設定は同社の質の高いサービスとインフラ投資を反映していると説明した。フェデックスはコメント要請に応じていない。両社は今週、四半期決算を発表する予定だ。

重いサーチャージ負担を小売業者はただ受け入れているだけなのか。

オントラック、ゴーフォー、ユニユニ、ジツ、ビーホなどは急成長中の配送会社だ。配送追跡・管理会社シップマトリックスのサティッシュ・ジンデル社長によると、米国の人口の約７０％をカバーしており、年末商戦期の荷物量の増加に対応するため、輸送能力も増強している。「輸送費を減らしたい多くの荷主に採用されている」という。

とはいえ、こうした企業の一部も高額な燃油サーチャージを導入している。オントラックが公開しているサーチャージ表によると、１０月２５日までの１週間の同社の西海岸のサーチャージは２９．５％だった。

輸送コストを抑えるために、米郵政公社（ＵＳＰＳ）やアマゾン・ドット・コムの物流部門を使う手もある。ＵＳＰＳは４月、大半の荷物に初めて８％の燃油サーチャージを課した。アマゾンも同じ月に、出品者向けのフルフィルメント手数料に３．５％の燃料・物流関連サーチャージを上乗せし始めた。

ただ配送会社の切り替えにはデメリットもあるとアナリストは指摘する。配送を複数社に分けると取扱量に応じた割引効果がなくなる可能性がある。また、年末商戦期の配送計画は数カ月前に決まるため、直前の変更は難しいという。ＪＰモルガンのアナリストは、アマゾンが近いうちにＵＰＳとフェデックスの市場支配を崩す可能性は低いとの見方を示した。
