items.title: News publishers contest new privacy law, fear impact on investigations
items.summary: News publishers argue the law could threaten investigative journalism, expose confidential sources and force the removal of factual reports ...
items.body:
Home / India News / News publishers contest new privacy law, fear impact on investigations

News publishers contest new privacy law, fear impact on investigations News publishers argue the law could threaten investigative journalism, expose confidential sources and force the removal of factual reports

Supreme Court of India

Reuters New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 26 2026 | 11:05 PM IST

Listen to This Article

A group of 21 news publishers, including companies owned by billionaires Mukesh Ambani and Gautam Adani, has challenged India's privacy law in court, arguing it would trample investigative work and let New Delhi identify journalists' sources, documents show.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government last year announced implementation of a privacy law to protect digital personal data of users, raising compliance requirements for platforms like Meta and Google. The publishers have said that since media outlets were not exempt, the law was an invasion of press freedom.
Media companies received assurances in an August meeting with the government that the law would protect press freedom, but not having a written carve-out for journalists like in the European Union, Singapore and Britain was alarming, India's Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) said in a confidential filing at the Supreme Court, reviewed by Reuters.
 

The October 6 lawsuit, being reported for the first time and due to be heard on Tuesday, is the most high-profile challenge to Modi's privacy law. Until now, only free speech activists and a group of smaller news outlets had challenged it.
It also marks an unusual challenge to the government from businesses headed by Ambani and Adani, who opposition parties allege are close to Modi and get favourable treatment - charges the businesses and the government vehemently deny.
Also Read

Can the CEC face prosecution? What the law says on accountability, immunity

BCI chairman Manan Kumar Mishra apologises to law students over NALSAR row

Govt tells Meta to ensure strict adherence to Indian law, content rules

Can an FIR simply be withdrawn? Why Neet protest cases may take time

NYT files motion to quash DOJ subpoenas over Air Force One coverage

DNPA and the media groups did not respond to requests for comment from Reuters, and neither did India's information technology ministry.
The publishers are demanding that most of the law's contentious provisions, which kick in from May 2027, should be quashed. They are arguing the law could force a journalist to get prior consent from a person they want to investigate and force publishers to erase stories. They also say powers granted by the law to demand information could expose reporters' sources.

The law would "render investigative journalism a benign and neutered recorder of events," the 698-page filing said. The provisions "constitute pre-censorship which is anathema to any democracy worth its name".
The lawsuit comes amid accusations of declining press freedom in India since Modi took office in 2014. Critics say many mainstream media outlets have not done enough to scrutinise Modi's government.
India's ranking in Reporters Without Borders' World Press Freedom Index fell to 157th out of 180 countries this year, from 140th in 2014 - but the government rejects the rankings.
Modi's government says it respects press freedom and says India, which has a "vibrant press and media ecosystem" of hundreds of newspapers and TV channels, does not need validation from foreign bodies.

Concerns over consent   DNPA's members include Ambani's Network18, which has seven digital news platforms, Adani's NDTV and other marquee media groups including the Indian Express and Times Internet, which is part of the Times of India group, publisher of India's largest-selling English-language daily.
A key concern in the law is the requirement of consent, the group's filing says.
A social media platform or online retailer can seek consent from users when they sign up, but the DNPA has argued that requiring a journalist to notify the subject of an investigation and seek consent "would allow that subject to destroy evidence, intimidate witnesses".
The law also lets people withdraw consent at any time and demand that their data be erased, without any public-interest safeguard, which DNPA says could force its members to unpublish or heavily redact a factual news report.

Fear of sources at risk
News publishers are concerned that a federal authority created under the law can impose fines for non-compliance, and grants powers to New Delhi to block access to any information in the "interests of the general public", which would curtail press freedom, DNPA said.
In an August letter to the government attached to the lawsuit, the group said India "has chosen to grant broad exemptions to the state, while failing to extend any corresponding protection to the press". No response was cited.
From next year, the law will also let New Delhi order any organization handling personal data "to furnish such information as it may call for", putting newsrooms at risk of having to divulge sources, the filing said.

It can also deter whistleblowers from sharing information on corruption, corporate wrongdoing or electoral malpractice with reporters, the DNPA argued.
The "nakedly unguided" provision must be quashed, the DNPA said, adding that the power "can extend to privileged communications in possession of a reporter or the informant."
(Reporting by Aditya Kalra)

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

items.title: Euro cae antes de reuniones de bancos centrales; el real brasileño se hunde
items.author: Chibuike Oguh
items.creator: Chibuike Oguh
items.summary: El euro cayó frente al dólar el lunes, ante una semana repleta de reuniones de los bancos centrales y con los precios del crudo aún en niveles elevados, mientras que el real brasileño se desplomó tras la sorprendente victoria electoral del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
items.body:
El euro cayó frente al dólar el lunes, ante una semana repleta de reuniones de los bancos centrales y con los precios del crudo aún en niveles elevados, mientras que el real brasileño se desplomó tras la sorprendente victoria electoral del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
* El euro se vio presionado la semana pasada, ya que una ola de ventas de bonos del Estado francés llevó la prima de riesgo de la deuda del país a su nivel más alto desde la crisis de la deuda soberana de 2011, lo que reavivó las preocupaciones sobre una nueva crisis financiera en toda la zona euro.
* Sin embargo, los precios de los bonos del Estado francés (OAT) subieron el lunes después de que Moody’s evitó la semana pasada una rebaja de la calificación crediticia de Francia, lo que alivió la presión sobre un Gobierno que lucha por reforzar sus finanzas.
* El euro bajó un 0,21% frente a la moneda estadounidense, a 1,1179 dólares , pero subió un 0,31% ante su par japonés, a 176,04 yenes .
* Los futuros del crudo Brent retrocedieron, pero se mantuvieron cerca de máximos de seis meses. Los elevados precios del petróleo lastran a las economías dependientes de las importaciones, como la zona euro. El Brent cayeron un 0,78%, a 115,81 dólares por barril.
* El dólar se ha visto respaldado por unos indicadores económicos estadounidenses resistentes, a pesar de los obstáculos, entre ellos el aumento de la inflación. La moneda estadounidense se vio sometida a presiones vendedoras durante la corrección del mercado impulsada por el sector tecnológico la semana pasada.
* Cinco bancos centrales importantes anunciarán sus decisiones de política monetaria a lo largo de esta semana. Se espera que la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos, el Banco Central Europeo y el Banco de Japón mantengan las tasas de interés sin cambios a pesar de las presiones inflacionarias.
* El yen japonés cayó un 0,43%, a 157,46 unidades por dólar.
* El índice dólar , que mide el comportamiento de la moneda estadounidense frente a una cesta de seis divisas, subió un 0,43%, a 102 unidades.
* Mientras, el real brasileño se desplomó frente al dólar después de que Lula logró el domingo un histórico cuarto mandato frente al senador Flávio Bolsonaro, hijo mayor del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro.
* El real cedió un 8,36%, a 5,4066 unidades por dólar, después de perder hasta un 12% más temprano.

items.title: TSX rises as investors welcome British Columbia election result
items.author: Fergal Smith
items.creator: Fergal Smith
items.summary: Canada's main stock index rebounded on Monday, led by financial and resource shares, after the result of British Columbia's provincial election potentially raised prospects for oil and gas companies.
items.body:
Canada's main stock index rebounded on Monday, led by financial and resource shares, after the result of British Columbia's provincial election potentially raised prospects for oil and gas companies.
The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) ended up 155.98 points, or 0.4%, at 35,944.16, after posting on Friday its lowest closing level since October 14.
The opposition Conservative Party won an [USN:L6N46B033 TEXT:"election"] in the province of British Columbia for the first time in nearly 100 years, promising to ramp up liquefied natural gas production.
"People are talking about the BC elections," said Barry Schwartz, chief investment officer at Baskin Wealth Management. "For oil and gas and construction companies, it's directionally positive."
The energy sector (.SPTTEN) , which includes a number of companies with a market capitalization greater than C$100 billion ($71.34 billion), such as Canadian Natural Resources (CNQ.TO) and Suncor Energy (SU.TO) , rose 0.4%.
[USN:L2N46B09G TEXT:"US crude oil futures"] settled 1.5% lower but remained elevated at $101.76 a barrel.
"The longer oil stays at these levels, you kind of have to own a CNQ or Suncor," Schwartz said.
The materials group (.GSPTTMT) , which includes metal mining shares, was up 0.7%. [USN:L2N46C0OI TEXT:"Gold"] rebounded from the previous session's more than three-month low as the drop in oil tempered inflation concerns ahead of a US Federal Reserve policy decision on Wednesday.
Heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) rose 0.8% and industrials (.GSPTTIN) ended 0.5% higher.
[USN:L6N46C0RN TEXT:"CAE"] (CAE.TO) said it will sell Flightscape, its airline operations software business, to fellow global aviation technology firm SITA in a deal valued at $500 million, including debt. Shares of CAE rose 4.6%.
Algoma Steel (ASTL.TO) ended 2.6% higher. The United States and Canada are working on a [USN:L6N46C11U TEXT:"deal"] to ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and autos, two US and four Canadian sources said.
Five of the 10 major sectors ended lower, including consumer discretionary (.GSPTTCD) . It lost 0.6%, with shares of clothing retailer Aritzia (ATZ.TO) down 2.3%.
($1 = 1.4018 Canadian dollars)

items.title: Ambani, Adani outlets among Indian publishers contesting Modi’s privacy law
items.author: Aditya Kalra
items.creator: Aditya Kalra
items.summary: A group of 21 news publishers, including companies owned by billionaires Mukesh Ambani and Gautam Adani, has challenged India's privacy law in court, arguing it would trample investigative work and let New Delhi identify journalists' sources, documents show.
items.body:
A group of 21 news publishers, including companies owned by billionaires Mukesh Ambani and Gautam Adani, has challenged India's privacy law in court, arguing it would trample investigative work and let New Delhi identify journalists' sources, documents show.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government last year announced implementation of a privacy law to [USN:L4N3WQ0V8 TEXT:"protect digital personal data"] of users, raising compliance requirements for platforms like Meta and Google. The publishers have said that since media outlets were not exempt, the law was an invasion of press freedom.
Media companies received assurances in an August meeting with the government that the law would protect press freedom, but not having a written carve-out for journalists like in the European Union, Singapore and Britain was alarming, India's Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) said in a confidential filing at the Supreme Court, reviewed by Reuters.
The October 6 lawsuit, being reported for the first time and due to be heard on Tuesday, is the most high-profile challenge to Modi’s privacy law. Until now, only free speech activists and a group of smaller news outlets had [USN:L4N3ZZ10J TEXT:"challenged"] it.
It also marks an unusual challenge to the government from businesses headed by Ambani and Adani, who opposition parties allege are close to Modi and get favourable treatment - charges the businesses and the government vehemently deny.
DNPA and the media groups did not respond to requests for comment from Reuters, and neither did India's information technology ministry.
The publishers are demanding that most of the law's contentious provisions, which kick in from May 2027, should be quashed. They are arguing the law could force a journalist to get prior consent from a person they want to investigate and force publishers to erase stories. They also say powers granted by the law to demand information could expose reporters' sources.
The law would "render investigative journalism a benign and neutered recorder of events," the 698-page filing said. The provisions "constitute pre-censorship which is anathema to any democracy worth its name".
The lawsuit comes amid accusations of declining press freedom in India since Modi took office in 2014. Critics say many mainstream media outlets have [USN:L4N43Q0BR TEXT:"not done enough"] to scrutinise Modi’s government.
India's ranking in Reporters Without Borders’ World Press Freedom Index fell to 157th out of 180 countries this year, from 140th in 2014 - but the government rejects the rankings.
Modi's government says it respects press freedom and says India, which has a "vibrant press and media ecosystem" of hundreds of newspapers and TV channels, does not need validation from foreign bodies.
CONCERNS OVER CONSENT DNPA's members include Ambani's Network18, which has seven digital news platforms, Adani's NDTV (NDTV.NS) and other marquee media groups including the Indian Express and Times Internet, which is part of the Times of India group, publisher of India's largest-selling English-language daily.
A key concern in the law is the requirement of consent, the group's filing says.
A social media platform or online retailer can seek consent from users when they sign up, but the DNPA has argued that requiring a journalist to notify the subject of an investigation and seek consent "would allow that subject to destroy evidence, intimidate witnesses".
The law also lets people withdraw consent at any time and demand that their data be erased, without any public-interest safeguard, which DNPA says could force its members to unpublish or heavily redact a factual news report.
FEAR OF SOURCES AT RISK News publishers are concerned that a federal authority created under the law can impose fines for non-compliance, and grants powers to New Delhi to block access to any information in the "interests of the general public", which would curtail press freedom, DNPA said.
In an August letter to the government attached to the lawsuit, the group said India "has chosen to grant broad exemptions to the state, while failing to extend any corresponding protection to the press". No response was cited.
From next year, the law will also let New Delhi order any organization handling personal data “to furnish such information as it may call for”, putting newsrooms at risk of having to divulge sources, the filing said.
It can also deter whistleblowers from sharing information on corruption, corporate wrongdoing or electoral malpractice with reporters, the DNPA argued.
The “nakedly unguided” provision must be quashed, the DNPA said, adding that the power “can extend to privileged communications in possession of a reporter or the informant.”

items.title: After Vucic defeat, Serbia waits to learn how student-backed leaders will govern
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Serbia woke to a new era on Monday after a student-backed protest movement unseated longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic in a historic landslide election.
items.body:
Serbia woke to a new era on Monday after a student-backed protest movement unseated longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic in a [USN:L6N46B017 TEXT:"historic landslide election"] that sparked nationwide celebrations, although few had an idea of how they would govern.
Tens of thousands [USN:L6N46B0A6 TEXT:"took to the streets"] of Belgrade and other cities and towns across Serbia after Vucic conceded defeat late on Sunday, capping two years of peaceful anti-government protests calling for the populist ruler to step down.
With almost 99% of votes counted, the students' candidates had secured a commanding 52.7% of the vote, according to the State Election Commission, versus 39.2% for Vucic's Serbia Progressive Party (SNS)-led alliance.
That gives the students 139 seats in the 250-seat parliament, leaving the SNS alliance with 97, and the remainder held by minority parties. The constitution allows up to 90 days for the creation of a government, once the parliament is convened after the announcement of final results by the state election commission.
"I thought it was unbelievable, I still do not believe it. It was too long, and (Vucic) was pressuring us for a long, long time," said university administrator Marijana Radovanovic Pajovic.
Vucic dominated Serbian politics as prime minister or president from 2014. But he was swept from power by a list of student-backed candidates [USN:L8N4650K6 TEXT:"born out of anti-corruption protests"] following the deaths of 16 people in the collapse of a train station canopy in the city of Novi Sad.
PROFOUND POLITICAL SHIFT The students' win marks a [USN:L8N4612LD TEXT:"profound political shift"] in the country of some 6 million people and is reminiscent of the [USN:L1N40V01B TEXT:"defeat of Hungary's Viktor Orban"] in April. It may also offer inspiration to other [USN:L2N46A01A TEXT:"student movements"] that have [USN:L5N46B060 TEXT:"cropped up"] across Europe in recent weeks demanding better education standards and prospects.
While the students' candidates include university professors, actors and farmers, the movement is without a leader - a strategy employed during protests to avoid any smear attempts by the government. It is unclear who will become prime minister and assume other key positions in order to enact the students' domestic agenda, which aims to root out graft and improve schooling, and manage the [USN:L6N46C0IX TEXT:"country's place on the international stage"].
"This corruption that has entered into all pores of our lives...of course it will change, we are hoping we will slowly go into that direction of a normal community," said 60-year-old insurance worker Svetlana Karagkozidou.
Prominent figures include the head of the students' candidate list, cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic, former central bank governor Dejan Soskic and Radomir Sajcic, a professor at Belgrade University, who spoke on behalf of the students following their victory.
However, not everyone welcomed the change.
"Changing the country like that so suddenly and all at once, I don’t like it. I don’t even know who is standing behind, who those people are, who will be leading the country," said 60-year-old civil worker Senka Radakovic.
Meanwhile, supporters of the student movement set about cleaning up a park near the parliament building in Belgrade that had long been used as a camp by Vucic's supporters. They removed metal barricades and tents and cleaned stickers off children's play equipment.
"I think it is one of Belgrade's most beautiful parks, that they took from us for a year or a year-and-a-half, and this is the least we can do right now," said one of the cleaning volunteers Filip Beselinovic.
Vucic and the SNS repeatedly denied [USN:L8N4612LD TEXT:"accusations of repression and corruption"].

items.title: Equities end higher as Anthropic's IPO filing buoys AI stocks
items.author: Chuck Mikolajczak, Shashwat Chauhan
items.creator: Chuck Mikolajczak, Shashwat Chauhan
items.summary: US stocks closed higher on Monday, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq coming off consecutive weekly declines, as Anthropic's IPO filing helped boost sentiment in AI-related stocks in a week filled with a host of market catalysts.
items.body:
US stocks closed higher on Monday, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq coming off consecutive weekly declines, as Anthropic's IPO filing helped boost sentiment in AI-related stocks in a week filled with a host of market catalysts.
[USN:L3N46C10M TEXT:"Anthropic disclosed"] steep losses and red-hot revenue growth in its filing for a US initial public offering, laying out its ambition to build AI systems capable of reshaping the global economy despite the high costs of developing the technology.
The AI lab is pushing ahead with its listing plans even as a once-lively autumn IPO calendar has slowed, with recent market volatility prompting companies to delay offerings.
Anthropic's filing comes as investors increasingly dissect the potential payoff from massive AI spending and at the start of an eventful week. On tap are the Federal Reserve's policy statement on Wednesday, readings on economic growth and inflation on Thursday and a slew of corporate earnings reports throughout the week.
More than a third of S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report earnings this week, including hyperscalers Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , whose results will be [USN:L6N45T17Q TEXT:"parsed for signs"] of whether the hefty AI investments are translating into growth.
"Today's all about the Anthropic release, so we're back on a little bit of an optimistic tilt, I would say. But there's a lot in that release. It will be interesting to see how well things are received when they actually come to list," said JP Powers, chief investment officer at RWA Wealth Partners in Boston.
"The risk is maybe a little bit of a whipsaw if things aren't all moving in the same direction. A little optimism today, but who knows what will happen from some of these other releases this week," he said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 146.42 points, or 0.28%, to 52,361.58, the S&P 500 (.SPX) gained 53.09 points, or 0.70%, to 7,676.77 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) gained 214.04 points, or 0.83%, to 26,169.38.
Semiconductor and chip-related companies, widely viewed as some of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, helped fuel the gains. The broader Philadelphia chips index (.SOX) was up 2.8% on the day but is still down 12.2% on the month.
Meta shares closed down 1.9% after the social media company said it [USN:L3N46C0RT TEXT:"plans to raise"] up to $95 billion in equity to fund its AI-related expansion of data centers, cloud computing power and other infrastructure.
The AI trade has come under pressure this month amid concerns that debt-funded spending may become harder to justify in the face of climbing borrowing costs.
The Anthropic filing helped buoy sentiment, however, as neocloud firms, including CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , erased earlier declines.
Other AI-linked companies, including photonic product makers Lumentum (LITE.O) and Coherent (COHR.N) , were among the best-performing S&P 500 stocks. Lumentum and Coherent gained about 8% and 6%, respectively. The technology index (.SPLRCT) led gains among the 11 major S&P 500 sectors, climbing 1.5%.
Megacap and growth stocks were also mostly higher. Tesla (TSLA.O) jumped 5.2% to close at its highest level in more than three months after Barclays upgraded its rating on the stock to "overweight" from "equal-weight."
Markets are pricing in only a 12.7% chance of a rate hike from the Fed on Wednesday, according to CME FedWatch. But with inflation pressures showing no signs of abating, market [USN:L6N46518P TEXT:"participants do not believe"] the central bank will be on hold for long.
Investors are also bracing for the November 3 midterm elections , which will decide control of the US Congress.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.36-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange and by a 1.09-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.
The S&P 500 posted seven new 52-week highs and seven new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 82 new highs and 349 new lows.
Volume on US exchanges was 16.7 billion shares, compared with the 17.2 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

items.title: Officials from Mecca pact countries to meet Iranian officials in Tehran
items.author: CNA
items.summary: This will be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the three-nation bloc since Saudi Arabia was drawn deeper into the wider Iran conflict.
items.body:

Officials from Mecca pact countries to meet Iranian officials in Tehran

This will be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the three-nation bloc since Saudi Arabia was drawn deeper into the wider Iran conflict.

Mecca defence pact meeting between Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Oct 5, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Saudi Press Agency)

FAST

Top officials from Mecca Pact countries Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan are to meet Iran's leaders in Tehran on Monday (Oct 26) in their first high-level contact since the kingdom became a pressure point in the wider Iran conflict.

Saudi Arabia will be represented by Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan by army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Turkiye by intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, Saudi and Iranian officials said.

Attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have spiralled in recent weeks and rhetoric between Washington and Tehran has grown more heated. Both countries have also drawn up plans to restart the wider war, possibly after the US midterm elections on Nov 3.

Monday's planned talks will be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the three-nation bloc since Saudi Arabia was drawn deeper into the conflict. Under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed in August, an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said on Monday discussions on regional security would include "Israel’s expansionist policies, developments in the Palestinian territories and Lebanon, and the repercussions of US and Israeli military action against Iran."

Baghaei said the meeting, proposed during a visit by Munir to Tehran last week, could be a first step towards establishing regional security mechanisms based on the interests of countries in the region.

Related:

CNA Explains: What is the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement?

Commentary: How far will Pakistan go in defending Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks?

(From left) Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif pose after signing a joint defence agreement in Mecca, Saudi Arabia on Aug 7, 2026. (Photo: Saudi Press Agency/Handout via Reuters)

Qatari mediators met Iranian officials in Tehran on Sunday in a push to de-escalate regional tensions, Reuters reported. Qatar has, for months, played a mediating role between Tehran and Washington.

A senior Iranian official said the meeting was initiated by Pakistan, during Munir's visit to Tehran, as he met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other senior officials. During the visit, Iranian officials told him there would be no talks with Washington until Tehran's demands were met, according to Iranian media.

Earlier mediation efforts involving both Pakistan and Qatar helped produce an interim peace agreement in June, but the deal quickly unravelled as fighting between Iran and the United States resumed weeks later.

The deputy secretary of Iran's top security body, Ali Baqeri-Kani, told state TV that Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid, Pakistan's Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin would visit Tehran for consultations with Iran’s Supreme National Security Council on regional security.

Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said the meeting is part of ongoing efforts by the Mecca Pact countries to de-escalate the current crisis, promote diplomatic solutions, and support mediation efforts led by Qatar and Pakistan.

"The visit also underscores the pivotal role of the Mecca Pact states in fostering regional security and stability, and their commitment to working with all nations in the region toward achieving this goal," Krimly posted on X.

Pakistan's military media wing and Turkiye's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Related:

UK to deploy fighter jets to help protect Saudi from Houthi attacks

Türkiye sending technical, defensive support to Saudi Arabia to help fight Houthis, officials say

TENSIONS RISING Saudi Arabia intercepted another wave of missiles and drones on Sunday as fighting with the Houthis continued unabated.
Ministers from the Mecca Pact countries held an emergency meeting in Riyadh earlier this month and agreed to ensure the "rapid deployment" of military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia.

The Houthi attacks have become an increasingly destabilising element in the US-Israeli conflict with Iran, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in the wider war.

Tensions between Washington and Tehran have sharpened in recent days. President Donald Trump said on Friday the US may carry out another military operation against Iran and Iran's leaders have said that a renewed US military campaign would be met with a stronger response than before.

Iranian security officials have told Reuters that Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if the United States and Israel attack again. A US intelligence memo this week warned that Iranian plots against American personnel had reached "advanced stages".

The war, now nearly eight months old, has weighed on President Donald Trump's approval ratings ahead of the midterms.

The Mecca agreement's first article says the parties shall use "all necessary means" to eliminate threats to one another's territorial integrity, sovereignty or internationally recognised borders, according to a text seen by Reuters.

Efforts by Turkiye’s parliament to ratify the agreement began last week and are still underway, while Pakistan approved the pact last week.

Source: Reuters/ia

Yoshifumi Takemoto　Tamiyuki Kihara

［東京　２６日　ロイター］ - 高市早苗首相は２６日、サイバーセキュリティに関する関係閣僚会議で、相次ぐサイバー攻撃に対処するため、来週中を目途に政府の緊急対策パッケージをまとめる方針を明らかにした。

首相は会議で、赤沢亮正経産相や古川俊治サイバー安全保障担当相に対し、国家サイバー統括室（ＮＣＯ）への情報集約徹底や想定されるリスクに関する情報発信などを指示した。

さらにＮＣＯに情報を集約し、想定される脅威やリスクに応じて経営層、専門家、国民向けなど対象を明確にした情報発信を強化すること、サプライチェーン全体でサイバー攻撃の観測網を整備し、中小企業を含めた迅速な対策につなげる取り組みを前倒しで実施しすることなども指示した。

そのうえで、実態を解明したサイバー攻撃に対してはアクセス無害化措置も含め、あらゆる対処オプションを戦略的に選択し、実行するとした。また、同盟国や海外の関係機関とも緊密に連携し、攻撃主体の特定など国際社会と一体となった取り組みを進めるよう要請した。

会議後、ＮＣＯの担当者が記者団の取材に応じ、一連のサイバー攻撃について「標的の調査や侵害にＡＩ（人工知能）を使用している可能性は高い」と説明。今後も同種の攻撃が続く恐れがあるとし、対応を急ぐ考えを示した。

（竹本能文、鬼原民幸　編集：石田仁志）

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ２６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ２６日 ロイター] - ラピダス（東京都千代田区）は２６日、インドに本社を置くグローバルテクノロジー企業、ＨＣＬテックと次世代半導体技術で協業すると発表した。ＨＣＬテックがベンガル―ルなどインド２カ所に開発センターを開設。ラピダスの将来的な人材ニーズに対応するため、インドでの半導体エンジニア育成・確保でも協力する。

開発センターは、プロセス設計キット（ＰＤＫ）開発や、半導体の回路パターンを転写する際に使われる原版のマスク設計などの半導体エンジニアリング機能をラピダスに提供する。

ラピダスの小池淳義社長は「インドで拡大する半導体エンジニアリング人材の活用が可能となり、日本での事業運営を補完する専任の開発体制を構築できると期待している」とコメントした。

items.author: Jonathan Levin

items.summary: Earnings season is upon us, and Wall Street expects companies in the S&P 500 Index that aren’t tied to artificial intelligence to rake in profits. That would be good news if it pointed to a broadening out of earnings growth, but instead the gauge is in a Pyrrhic boom created by President Donald Trump’s war with Iran. It’s a bump that we’ll pay for later.

items.title: インタビュー：27年春闘は目線上げる、物価上昇を上回る賃上げから一歩先へ＝自動車総連会長
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Kentaro Sugiyama　Makiko Yamazaki

［東京　２６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Kentaro Sugiyama　Makiko Yamazaki

［東京　２６日　ロイター］ - 自動車総連の金子晃浩会長は２６日、ロイターとのインタビューで、２０２７年春闘に向けて、物価上昇を上回る賃上げの実現に加え、生産性向上や労働価値向上を賃金に反映させる一段高い視点が必要との考えを示した。

ここ数年の春闘は、急速な物価上昇を背景に「物価を上回る賃上げ」の実現が大きな目標となっていた。金子会長はその取り組みについて「生活防衛という面では一定の成果を上げた」と評価する一方、「物価上昇に追いつくだけで満足する取り組みではなく、それを土台として、さらに一段高い視点から付加価値や労働の価値に見合う賃上げを目指すべきだ」と語った。

自動車総連は、企業グループ別の労連が結集した組織で、１２労連・７８万人で構成される。２６年春闘では、中小労組の要求目安として月額１万２０００円以上のベースアップ（ベア）を掲げ、加盟組合のベア平均獲得額は過去最高の９７５２円となった。定期昇給込みの賃上げ率は４．８１％で、このうちベア寄与分は３．５８％だった。

金子会長は「物価上昇に見合うだけの取り組みを毎年続けても、成長にはつながらない」と指摘。日本の賃金水準が長期にわたって海外主要国に劣後している現状に危機感を示し、「付加価値や労働の価値に見合う賃上げを獲得して初めて人材の価値が高まり、日本の競争力向上につながる」と強調した。

その上で「今までより目線を上げる議論をしている」と説明。物価上昇分を補う賃上げだけでは海外との格差を縮めることはできず、生産性向上や人材への投資の成果を賃金に反映させることが重要との認識を示した。

日本の自動車産業を取り巻く環境は厳しさを増しているとの認識も示した。中国メーカーの台頭や人工知能（ＡＩ）の急速な進展を挙げ「日本企業が生き残り、存在感を維持し続けることは容易ではない」と語った。「コスト競争だけでは勝てない。人材への投資を通じて企画力や創造力を高めることが日本の勝ち筋だ」と述べた。

連合が単年度の賃上げ目標に加えて、今回から中期目標を設定したことについても「考え方は全く一緒だ」と評価。「目指す姿から逆算して必要な賃上げを考えるバックキャスティングの発想が重要だ」と述べ、労働界として中長期的な賃金ビジョンを持つ必要性を訴えた。

一方、連合が２２日に発表した２７年春闘の基本構想で、要求賃上げ率（定期昇給込み）を「６％中心、５％以上」としたことについては、「昨年までの取り組みと大きく変わるものではないが、『６％中心』を加えることで前進姿勢を示した」との見方を示した。その上で「大きな方向性として相違はない」と評価し、自動車総連としての具体的な要求方針は今後検討していく考えを示した。

発足２年目に入った高市早苗政権の政策については「経済成長に重点を置いて進めてきたことは評価している」と述べたほか、適正取引の推進などを通じた賃上げ環境の整備も評価した。一方で、「国力を上げていくためには、上だけでなく、下限を引き上げていくことも必要だ」とし、特定最低賃金の引き上げなど賃金底上げ策の強化に期待感を示した。

items.title: 中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝中国横ばい、主要中銀会合控え警戒感
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [上海 ２６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[上海 ２６日 ロイター] - 中国株式市場は、一時の下げから切り返し、おおむね横ばいで引けた。今週の主要中央銀行の決定会合を控え慎重姿勢が強まった。香港株は上昇した。

上海総合指数は０．２％高で終了。ＣＳＩ３００指数は４１０３．５４と、ほぼ変わらずだった。

ハイテク株が引き続き下げを主導した。深セン証券取引所の新興企業向け市場「創業板（チャイネクスト）」総合指数は１．７％安、上海証券取引所の新興ハイテク企業向け市場「科創板」５０指数は２．２％安となった。

ＣＳＩ５Ｇ通信指数は４％急落した。

石油・ガス株は上昇し、相場の下げを一部相殺した。同セクターの指数は２．４％上昇。米国とイランの緊張緩和への期待があるものの、主要産油国サウジアラビアへの攻撃が続き、投資家は警戒を維持した。

モルガン・スタンレーのアナリストはリポートで「信託課税に伴う売りへの懸念、電子商取引への圧力、マクロ経済の弱まり、世界市場のボラティリティーの高まりが中国市場の調整を加速させている」と指摘。「Ａ株市場にとって重要なのは、『国家隊』（政府系投資家 ）がいつ本格的に買いを正式に開始するかだ」と述べた。

香港市場では、ハンセン指数が０．５％上昇した一方、ハンセンテック指数は０．４％下落した。

モルガン・スタンレーのアナリストはリポートで「信託課税に伴う売りへの懸念、電子商取引への圧力、マクロ経済の弱まり、世界市場のボラティリティーの高まりが中国市場の調整を加速させている」と指摘。「Ａ株市場にとって重要なのは、『国家隊』（政府系投資家 ）がいつ本格的に買いを正式に開始するかだ」と述べた。

香港市場では、ハンセン指数が０．５％上昇した一方、ハンセンテック指数は０．４％下落した。

items.title: ロシア、首都防空網狙うドローン攻撃計画阻止　2人拘束
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［モスクワ　２６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［モスクワ　２６日　ロイター］ - ロシア連邦保安局（ＦＳＢ）は２６日、首都モスクワの防空システムの主要部や電力施設を国内からドローン（無人機）で攻撃するウクライナの計画を阻止し、計画に関与した男２人を拘束したと明らかにした。

２人は、南コーカサス地域出身。ウクライナ保安庁（ＳＢＵ）の指示を受けて、ロシア国内の２州でＦＰＶ（一人称視点）ドローンと爆発物を入手してモスクワ州に搬送し、ドローンを設定して起動させた。ドローンはウクライナから遠隔操作される予定だったという。

ＦＳＢは「容疑者の１人はＳＢＵ職員に勧誘され、金銭的報酬と引き換えに、指示に従って破壊・テロ攻撃の準備と実行のためにロシアへ入国したことが判明した。容疑者はこの目的のため、親しい知人の協力を得た」と説明。「電力インフラ施設やモスクワのミサイル防衛システムの主要要素の１つに対するテロ攻撃の実行を準備していた容疑者らを、ＦＳＢの職員が拘束した」とした。

ＳＢＵおよびウクライナ側からのコメントは直ちに得られていない。ロシアはウクライナの電力施設などのインフラへの攻撃を強化しているが、ウクライナもここ数カ月、ロシア首都に対するドローン攻撃の試みを活発化させている。

items.title: Meta eyes record $95 billion equity raise to fund AI infrastructure push
items.summary: Meta plans $35 billion in stock offerings and a further $60 billion share sale programme to finance AI expansion, as heavy infrastructure spending strains its free cash flow ...
items.body:
Home / World News / Meta eyes record $95 billion equity raise to fund AI infrastructure push

Meta eyes record $95 billion equity raise to fund AI infrastructure push Meta plans $35 billion in stock offerings and a further $60 billion share sale programme to finance AI expansion, as heavy infrastructure spending strains its free cash flow

Reuters 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 26 2026 | 9:42 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Meta Platforms said on Monday it plans to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising, as the social media giant spends heavily on its artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure expansion.
  The Facebook parent has launched public offerings worth about $35 billion in common and preferred stock and said it also plans to launch a separate at-the-market share sale programme worth up to $60 billion.
  The company will launch the larger share sale programme after its new non-voting Class C shares begin trading, which is expected in the first quarter of 2027, but said it has not yet finalised the timing and terms of the sale.
 

  Meta's fundraising plan, among the biggest by an AI company, has also drawn interest of up to $5 billion in total from Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom for Class A shares.
  Their funding interest adds to concerns about an increasingly circular flow of capital in the AI industry, as chip suppliers help finance the expansion of one of their biggest customers.
Also Read

Zuckerberg strikes Meta deal to cover potential California billionaire tax

Meta's $25 bn penalty marks a massive win for New Mexico's attorney general

US court orders Meta to pay $25 bn for misleading users on data privacy

Australian govt to sue Facebook, TikTok for alleged breaches of ban

Govt asks Meta to avoid algorithmic bias towards limited set of narratives

  Meta has been pouring money into chips and data centres to compete better with OpenAI and Anthropic.
  "We expect investors to continue to question the financing and potential for future capital raises," William Blair analysts said in a note.
  "Overall, we believe the financing reinforces both Meta's confidence in the long-term returns from AI investment and the increasingly capital-intensive nature of pursuing that opportunity."

  The company's shares fell about 1.4 per cent in morning trading.
  The latest fundraising further underscores a shift among big technology companies increasingly tapping debt markets and raising equity to bolster their AI infrastructure, having previously relied on cash to fund their investments.
  Earlier this year, Alphabet increased the size of its equity offerings to $84.75 billion.
  Separately on Monday, SpaceX said an affiliate of Apollo Global Management will buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the rockets-to-AI firm, in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion.
  META'S AI SPENDING IS BURNING CASH
  Meta has committed to spending about $825 billion in the future, primarily driven by its growing investments in data centres, AI-related infrastructure and cloud computing power.

  But the rapid expansion has eroded its historically strong free cash flow.
  The company reported a $2.12 billion cash burn in the third quarter, its first negative free cash flow in over a decade, compared with a positive cash flow of $10.63 billion a year ago.
  Still, the early popularity of its consumer-focused AI agent Muse and the release of a competitive new series of AI models have helped partly justify Meta's substantial investments.
  "We believe that Meta will ultimately produce a profitable AI business and its returns longer-term should help the company diversify, although the path may not be linear," William Blair analysts said.

  The company had cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $82.45 billion and long-term debt of $80.92 billion as of September 30, according to its latest quarterly filing.
  Last week, Meta raised the lower end of its annual capital expenditure forecast to a range of $135 billion to $145 billion.
  The company has said it would issue Class C common stock in January 2027, effectively resulting in a two-for-one split, to fund acquisitions and retain top talent while maintaining CEO Mark Zuckerberg's control.
  Meta agreed to grant Zuckerberg Class C shares that he can sell to help pay a potential California billionaire wealth tax, in exchange for a commitment to keep him in California.

items.title: 予算案で国防投資計画の全財源確保と英首相、ＮＡＴＯ目標への道筋も提示へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ロンドン　２６日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ロンドン　２６日　ロイター］ - バーナム英首相は２６日、ヒーリー財務相が今週、予算案を発表する際、既存の国防関連の公約を全額賄う財源計画を示すと述べた。２０３５年までの北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）の国防費目標を達成するための道筋も併せて示すという。

ヒーリー氏は２８日に就任後初の予算案を発表する予定だ。

バーナム氏はＩＴＶの番組「グッド・モーニング・ブリテン」で、政権が最初に取り組むべき課題は、既に発表した国防投資計画の財源を全額確保することだと説明。「その実現に向けて懸命に取り組んできた。財源の裏付けがあり、実行に移せる計画を持つことが極めて重要だ。どのように財源を確保したかについては、２８日に詳しく説明する」と述べた。

現在、国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比約２．６％の国防費を３０年までに３％、３５年までに３．５％に引き上げるという公約の道筋も２８日に示されるのかとの質問には、「含まれる。それを実現する上で正しいと考える方法を計画として示す」とし、「ＮＡＴＯへの公約は必ず果たす」と語った。

items.title: Musk says SpaceX raised $40 bn in debt deal, predicts neocloud shakeout
items.summary: Musk, in a post on X, attributed the successful debt raise to the company's investment-grade status and revenue from its Starlink satellite internet and launch businesses ...
items.body:
Home / World News / Musk says SpaceX raised $40 bn in debt deal, predicts neocloud shakeout

Musk says SpaceX raised $40 bn in debt deal, predicts neocloud shakeout Musk, in a post on X, attributed the successful debt raise to the company's investment-grade status and revenue from its Starlink satellite internet and launch businesses

For the fourth quarter, the company expects $35 billion to $40 billion in capital expenditure, according to Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 26 2026 | 9:32 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Elon Musk said on Sunday that SpaceX had closed $40 billion in debt financing for graphics processing units, underscoring the soaring cost of building AI computing capacity.
  Musk, in a post on X, attributed the successful debt raise to the company's investment-grade status and revenue from its Starlink satellite internet and launch businesses.
  It was not immediately clear from Musk's post what he meant by the deal being "closed" or whether investors had agreed to pricing for the debt.
  "This is primarily callable debt for GPU purchases that will arrive in Q1 and Q2. Not a major factor this quarter," Musk said in the post.  
 

For the fourth quarter, the company expects $35 billion to $40 billion in capital expenditure, according to Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen.
Also Read

Musk says he was behind Starlink speed curbs after Ukraine service restored

Ukraine says Starlink speed limits lifted after disruptions to military ops

Musk's donations top $445 million in push for Republicans in US midterms

Trump says Musk restored Ukraine's Starlink access, dodges call question

Trump admin offers mixed messages on limits to Ukraine's Starshield access

  Reuters reported earlier this month that SpaceX was in talks with banks and asset managers to raise $40 billion for the purchase of Nvidia artificial intelligence chips.
  The funding highlights the enormous capital requirement of the AI boom, as technology companies race to secure advanced processors and build out the computing infrastructure needed to support AI development.
  Musk said debt markets "have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers."

  As a result, he predicted neocloud companies would face significant consolidation and failures, and later said SpaceX won't buy any neoclouds, calling it "pointless."
  Unlike larger cloud firms that serve a broad range of industries, neoclouds such as Nebius and CoreWeave mostly focus on tech customers and offer capacity tailored for AI technology.
  Investors have started betting against US neocloud and data center companies, after fears that their debt-fueled AI buildout was becoming unsustainable sparked a selloff. 
AI investment, chip manufacturing   SpaceX's revenue climbed 161% from a year ago to $14.58 billion for the three months ended September 30. AI revenue surged by almost 10 times to $7.56 billion, the clearest evidence yet that SpaceX's heavy investment in AI was paying off.

  The shift is reshaping a company whose financial engine has long been its Starlink satellite internet services business and whose longer-term ambitions still hinge on getting Starship rockets into regular service.
  Terafab, the chip manufacturing joint venture between SpaceX and Tesla in Austin, should produce its first test chip around May or June of next year as it aims to reach volume production by the third quarter of 2028.
  Musk told investors in a conference call last week that a merger of his two companies would be "a good idea," citing growing overlap between them.
  Prior to its blockbuster IPO, SpaceX listed "manufacturing our own GPUs" among the substantial capital expenditures it is undertaking in its S-1 statement, warning prospective investors of its big spending plans to develop AI and other technologies.

items.title: 企業の「悲鳴」に政府どう対応、止まらぬサイバー攻撃　来週にも緊急対策と首相
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ２６日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ２６日 ロイター] - ９月ごろから急増した企業などへのサイバー攻撃は収まる気配がなく、ＧＭＯインターネットグループが政府に「能動的サイバー防御」の発動を要請する事態に発展した。不正アクセスによる情報流出が相次ぐ中、顧客に一律の補償金を支払う企業も出ており、政府は２６日夕、サイバーセキュリティーに関する関係閣僚会議を開いた。来週中にも緊急対策パッケージをまとめる方針で、専門家からは能動的サイバー防御の運用指針を示すなどして政府が抑止力を発揮すべきだとの声が上がっている。

「個別のサイバー攻撃事案については、政府の対応状況を攻撃者に知らせることにもつながるため、コメントは差し控える」。ＧＭＯの要請への対応を問われた木原稔官房長官は２６日午前の記者会見でこう述べた。その上で、企業から要請があるかどうかにかかわらず、「法律の要件に照らして適切に判断される」と説明した。

自社のＦＸ（外国為替証拠金取引）自動売買サービスがサイバー攻撃を受けたＧＭＯインターネットＧには、一部ユーザーから身に覚えのない取引が行われたとの報告が寄せられている。攻撃者とみられる相手から５０００万ドル（約７９億円）を要求されているほか、応じなければ自社や顧客の情報を公開するとの連絡も受けているという。同社株は２６日、取引開始直後から売り込まれ、前営業日比１５％安で引けた。

岩井コスモ証券投資調査部の有沢正一フェローはＧＭＯの要請について、「これは政府に助けを求める企業側の『悲鳴』だ」と指摘する。「個別事案には対処できないと言うだけで終わるのか。政府の対応が注目される」と話した。同証券も売買管理システムがサイバー攻撃を受け、顧客の意図しない売買注文の発注が確認されるなどの被害を受けた。 

今月１日に施行されたサイバー対処能力強化法と関連整備法により、サイバー攻撃による重大な被害を防止するため、警察や自衛隊が攻撃者のサーバーなどに対して無害化措置を講じる「能動的サイバー防御」が可能になった。有沢氏は「運用方針が明確に示され、広く認知されれば、それ自体が抑止力となる可能性がある」とみる。

高市早苗首相は２６日夕に開いた関係閣僚会議で、来週中をめどに政府の緊急対策パッケージをまとめる考えを表明した。システムの脆弱性を発見する模擬的な攻撃テストを行うことや、サプライチェーン（供給網）全体でサイバー攻撃の観測網を整備し、中小企業を含めた迅速な対策につなげる取り組みを前倒しで実施することなどを指示した。

＜攻撃は業種選ばず、マクロ経済全体の損失も＞

トレンドＡＩのデータによると、日本に拠点を置く組織で発生したサイバーセキュリティー事案は今年、１０月２０日時点で７２３件と、昨年通年の５９４件をすでに上回った。１０月だけで１１１件に達したという。有沢氏は「直接資金を狙うなら金融機関が主な標的となるが、ランサムウェアの場合は業種を選ばない」と話した。

第一ライフ資産運用経済研究所の前田和馬・経済調査部主席エコノミストは、サイバー攻撃の影響が単一企業にとどまる場合は競合他社による代替などでマクロ経済への影響は限定的としながらも、交通インフラのように代替が難しい事業者や産業全体に被害が広がった場合には、「マクロ経済全体の損失に波及する可能性がある」と指摘する。

広く利用されているプログラミング言語「ＰＨＰ」で重大な脆弱性が見つかった問題では、日本企業が相次いでウェブサイトの機能を停止した。外食業界ではテイクアウト注文の受け付けを見合わせる動きが広がり、一時的ながら経済活動に一定の影響が出た。

一方、前田氏はサイバーセキュリティー対策強化に伴うＩＴ関連支出の増加は、国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）を押し上げる可能性が高いとみる。２０００年問題への対応では、全世界のＩＴ対策費用が３０００億━６０００億ドル（約４７兆─９４兆円）に達し、１９９９年の世界ＧＤＰの０．９─１．８％に相当したとされる。

サイバーセキュリティー関連企業への関心も高まっている。トレンドマイクロ株は８月中旬の５３００円台から足元では７６００円台まで上昇した。今週から決算発表が本格化する中、各社経営陣によるサイバーセキュリティー対策や業績への影響に関する発言にも注目が集まりそうだ。

items.title: China proposes measures against foreign entities' infringement of trade secrets
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: China's commerce ministry released on Monday draft regulations for protecting trade secrets, proposing measures against foreign entities whose actions endanger or pose a real threat to China's national sovereignty, security or development interests.
items.body:
China's commerce ministry released on Monday draft regulations for protecting trade secrets, proposing measures against foreign entities whose actions endanger or pose a real threat to China's national sovereignty, security or development interests.
The measures include restricting or banning the entities from making new investment in China and from importing or exporting goods and technologies related to China, according to the draft.
The ministry is seeking public feedback on the draft regulations until November 24, it said in a statement.

items.body:
明治安田、英マン・グループの株式5％取得へ　投資も拡大
10/26 17:24 配信

写真は明治安田生命保険本社の看板。5月14日、都内で撮影。 REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon

［東京　２６日　ロイター］ - 明治安田生命保険は２６日、英運用大手マン・グループと新たな戦略提携を結び、発行済み株式の約５％を市場から取得する予定だと発表した。今後３年間で総額２０００億円の投資・運用委託も目指す。

２０２５年２月に公表した戦略提携のもと、プライベートアセットを中心に協業を進めてきたが、対象領域を拡大する。マン・グループが提供する幅広い運用商品への投資機会の活用、クオンツ・人工知能（ＡＩ）を含む先進的資産運用手法に関する知見の共有などに取り組む。

items.body:
コーエーテクモ、通期の純利益を上方修正　年間配当56円に
10/26 17:15 配信

[東京 ２６日 ロイター] - ゲーム大手のコーエーテクモホールディングスは２６日、２０２７年３月期の連結純利益予想を従来の３１０億円から３７０億円（前年比１３．６％減） に上方修正した。年間配当予想も１株当たり４８円から５６円に上方修正した。

・中間連結業績が当初予想を上回り、為替前提見直しと事業・市場環境も反映。

・純利益予想はＩＢＥＳがまとめたアナリスト１２人の予想平均値の３５７億円を上回った。

・営業利益予想も従来の３２０億円から３４０億円に引き上げ。

・利益還元の基本方針として、配当金に自社株買いを加えた連結年間総配分性向５０％、または１株当たり年間配当５０円としており、最近の業績動向を踏まえ配当予想を引き上げ。前期は年間６６円。

・４─９月期の純利益は前年比３８．１％増の１８５億円で、中間期として過去最高。「ぽこ あ ポケモン」が世界販売本数５００万本を突破するなど、大型タイトルがけん引。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: 中国株式市場は、一時の下げから切り返し、おおむね横ばいで引けた。今週の主要中央銀行の決定会合を控え慎重姿勢が強まった。香...
items.body:
アジア株式市場サマリー：引け（26日）
10/26 16:53 配信

中国株式市場は、一時の下げから切り返し、おおむね横ばいで引けた。今週の主要中央銀行の決定会合を控え慎重姿勢が強まった。香港株は上昇した。

上海総合指数は０．２％高で終了。ＣＳＩ３００指数は４１０３．５４と、ほぼ変わらずだった。

ハイテク株が引き続き下げを主導した。深セン証券取引所の新興企業向け市場「創業板（チャイネクスト）」総合指数は１．７％安、上海証券取引所の新興ハイテク企業向け市場「科創板」５０指数は２．２％安となった。

ＣＳＩ５Ｇ通信指数は４％急落した。

石油・ガス株は上昇し、相場の下げを一部相殺した。同セクターの指数は２．４％上昇。米国とイランの緊張緩和への期待があるものの、主要産油国サウジアラビアへの攻撃が続き、投資家は警戒を維持した。

モルガン・スタンレーのアナリストはリポートで「信託課税に伴う売りへの懸念、電子商取引への圧力、マクロ経済の弱まり、世界市場のボラティリティーの高まりが中国市場の調整を加速させている」と指摘。「Ａ株市場にとって重要なのは、『国家隊』（政府系投資家 ）がいつ本格的に買いを正式に開始するかだ」と述べた。

香港市場では、ハンセン指数が０．５％上昇した一方、ハンセンテック指数は０．４％下落した。

ソウル株式市場は下落して引けた。今週の米ハイテク大手企業の決算発表を前に、人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株への投資を巡る懸念が強まった。

半導体大手のサムスン電子は１．１６％、同業のＳＫハイニックスは０．１６％、それぞれ下落した。

ＳＫハイニックスは、約１６兆ウォン（１２０億ドル）の特別配当を検討しているとの報道を受け、２８日の四半期決算発表に合わせて株主還元策を発表すると明らかにした。

取引された９１４銘柄のうち、１０１銘柄が上昇、７９２銘柄が下落した。

海外投資家は６９５５億ウォン相当を売り越した。

シドニー株式市場は小幅上昇で引けた。銀行株が下落したものの、鉱業株の上昇がこれを相殺し、下げから持ち直した。今週は、中央銀行の政策判断を左右する重要インフレ指標の発表を控えている。

Ｓ＆Ｐ／ＡＳＸ２００指数は一時０．８％下落した。

バンテージ・マーケッツの市場アナリスト、ヘベ・チェン氏は「銀行株は先週示されたディフェンシブ銘柄としての魅力がやや薄れている。投資家は利益を確定し、これまで売り込まれたセクターに目を向けているようだ」と述べた。

金融株指数は０．５％下落。四大銀行は０．３─０．８％安となった。

先週８％超下落した鉱業株指数は後、この日は２％近く上昇した。チェン氏は「先週の大幅な売りの後で割安株を買う動きが再び強まったことに加え、短期的なリスク選好の改善を反映している」と説明した。

主力のＢＨＰは１％高、リオティントは約０．２％高となった。

産金株指数は２．９％上昇し、６営業日ぶりに反発した。ノーザン・スター・リソーシズは２．８％上昇した。

市場は７─９月期のインフレ統計を待ち。物価上昇圧力が一段と強まれば、中銀の金利判断に影響する可能性がある。オーストラリア準備銀行（中央銀行）は１１月３日に政策判断を発表する予定。

市場が織り込む来週の利上げ確率は６５．５％、据え置き確率は３４．５％となっている。

データセンター運営のＮＥＸＴＤＣは１．３％下落。クレイグ・スクロギー最高経営責任者は、２０２７年度の賞与を辞退すると表明した。同社はその数日前に売上高見通しを引き下げ、今後の開発計画を一時停止した。

items.title: Trump says Brazil election looked 'rigged', defeated Bolsonaro's party recognizes Lula win
items.author: Oliver Griffin, Eduardo Simões
items.creator: Oliver Griffin, Eduardo Simões
items.summary: "I didn't take sides, but it looked like another rigged election," Trump told reporters, without providing any evidence. "It looked very bad to me."
items.body:
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's surprise win in [USN:L2N46B01X TEXT:"Brazil's presidential vote"] "looked like another rigged election," although the party of defeated right-winger Flavio Bolsonaro later acknowledged the result.
The son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, Flavio Bolsonaro has refused to concede defeat in [USN:L2N46B01X TEXT:"Sunday's presidential election"], saying he would seek the annulment of Lula's victory after the Supreme Court extended voting by two hours.
Later on Monday, however, Bolsonaro's Liberal Party said it [USN:S0N46906S TEXT:"acknowledged the runoff result"] in a statement signed by the party's head Valdemar Costa Neto.
"We recognize the presidential election results," Costa Neto said. "But we believe the issues raised need to be properly clarified."
Bolsonaro, who has not commented publicly since his party's statement, said earlier on Monday he would comply with a federal police order to hand over his passports following a visit to his father, who is under house arrest, and denied he was planning to flee Brazil.
Trump did not endorse Bolsonaro ahead of the vote, although Reuters has reported that officials from his State Department [USN:L1N4650X8 TEXT:"led a campaign"] to return the Bolsonaros to power.
"I didn't take sides, but it looked like another rigged election," Trump told reporters, without providing any evidence. "It looked very bad to me."
Bolsonaro lost to Lula by over 4 million votes, a clear result that it will be challenging for him to overturn. Fewer than 35,000 votes, or some 0.03% of the total, were cast in the extra two hours of voting ordered by the Supreme Court, according to an analysis of electoral records by Insper professor Pedro Burgos.
"I just think it had a very bad look, the election, the way it was tabulated," Trump said. "The extension given was very strange."
Vice President Geraldo Alckmin later defended Brazil's electoral system, saying in a TV interview with Rede Vanguarda that Trump's remarks were "totally wrong" and "unfounded."
Neither Trump nor Jair Bolsonaro accepted their election losses in 2020 and 2022, respectively. Brazil's former president was handed a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after losing to Lula.
Analysts do not expect Flavio Bolsonaro to be able to build the same anti-democratic movement as his father in 2022.
MARKETS ROILED BY LULA WIN World leaders have already widely congratulated Lula on his unprecedented fourth mandate, which was greeted with [USN:L2N46C051 TEXT:"dismay by investors"] who had been betting on a Bolsonaro win.
Brazil's real fell 8.1% against the dollar in its biggest one-day drop since 2002, while the stock exchange marked its steepest one-day fall since 2020.
"The initial selloff could moderate as election-related positions are unwound, but investors will demand convincing fiscal commitments before rebuilding exposure," said Pantheon Macroeconomics' chief Latin America economist Andres Abadia.
Lula's victory defied polls, precedent and global anti-incumbent sentiment to put the brakes on a wave of right-wing election victories across Latin America. He trailed Bolsonaro in the first round, but managed to convince voters to come out for him in the runoff.
Pollsters said a higher-than-expected turnout and an improved [USN:L6N46815Z TEXT:"social media campaign"] helped power Lula to victory.
During the campaign, Lula pointed to his track record of cutting poverty and inequality while also highlighting record-low unemployment, illiteracy and deforestation, but his fourth term may prove challenging.
He will face an [USN:L6N46B06R TEXT:"uphill battle"] for his agenda in a Congress [USN:L6N45R137 TEXT:"packed with Bolsonaro allies"] after a surge of conservative voters in the first round of the general election pushed the Brazilian legislature further to the right.

items.creator: ロイター

［東京　２６日　ロイター］ - 住友生命保険は２０２６年度下期の一般勘定運用について、日本国債...
items.body:
円債は償還多く残高減、保険新契約対応では超長期債購入＝住友生命・26年度下期運用計画
10/26 16:06 配信

都内の住友生命本社で５月撮影。REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon

Tomo Uetake

［東京　２６日　ロイター］ - 住友生命保険は２０２６年度下期の一般勘定運用について、日本国債は過去に購入した低利回り債を売って利回りの高い債券に入れ替える取り組みが中心で、保有債券の償還を加味した残高はやや減少するとの計画を示した。ただ保険新契約への対応では超長期国債への投資も実施する。

泉忠和・運用企画部長が２６日、運用方針説明会で明らかにした。

同社の運用資産の主軸となる「日本国債等」は、上期に続き、保険金の確実な支払いに向けて保有する低利回り債券を利回りの高い債券に入れ替える取り組みと、一時払終身保険など新規の契約によって保険料が入った分で超長期の日本国債への投資を行う。保有債券の償還が多いため、残高としては「若干の減少」（泉氏）を見込んでいる。

日銀の金融政策について、住友生命では今年１２月と来年４月に追加利上げが実施されると想定。その後は金融環境への影響を見極めながら、ターミナルレート（到達金利）の想定レンジ１．７５─２．２５％の範囲内で利上げを判断するとのシナリオを描く。

国内金利については、日銀の追加利上げや積極財政による財政悪化懸念を背景に上昇方向だが、市場が織り込むターミナル金利も相応に高いため一段の金利上振れリスクは限定的で、年度末の１０年金利は３．１％（２６日時点は２．８％）、３０年金利は４．２％（２６日時点は３．８％）での着地を見込む。

金利が想定より上振れた場合でも「社債や株を売って日本国債を買うというようなオペレーションは、現状でバランスしている負債の金利感応度を引き上げることになるので、考えていない」（泉氏）という。

外国債券のうち、為替リスクをヘッジしないオープン外債は、上期に続き、残高を減らす計画。企業価値の持続的向上に向けたバランス運用の一環として、オープン外債から期待リターンの高い外国株式への一部資金のシフトも実施する。

ヘッジ付き外債のうち事業債は、収益性が低下した固定金利資産を削減し、プライベートクレジット等の変動金利資産を増やす計画。一方、ヘッジ付きソブリン債は、上期に続いて残高は横ばいとする方針。

政治と財政を巡る不安から足元で売り圧力が強まるフランス国債について、泉氏は「２０１６年度以降は外貨建てクレジットを強化しており、外国債は残高を伸ばしていない。残高はあるにはあるが、かなり僅少なウエートだ」と説明した。

内外株式は残高を増加、オルタナティブもインフラエクイティやＰＥ（プライベートエクイティ）ファンドへの段階的な投資により積み増しを計画。一方、不動産は、投資用不動産に選別投資するものの、上期に行った売却の影響で残高は減少を見込む。

住友生命の一般勘定の資産残高は、３月末時点で３７兆６５６０億円。うち外貨建て資産は１１兆８４１０億円（３１．４％）。

２０２６年度の相場見通し（レンジと年度末）は以下の通り。

日本国債１０年物利回り　　２．５０―３．３０％　（３．１０％）

日本国債３０年物利回り　　３．６０─４．６０％　（４．２０％）

items.body:
日経平均は小幅に3日続落、方向感出ず　イベント前の様子見で
10/26 16:06 配信

写真は2024年12月、都内の東京証券取引所で撮影。REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon

Hiroko Hamada

[東京 ２６日 ロイター] - 東京株式市場で日経平均は小幅に３日続落し、前営業日比０．８０％（５０３円５１銭）安の６万２１８９円６５銭で取引を終えた。米ハイパースケーラーや国内ハイテク企業の決算発表、日米の中銀イベントを控える中、様子見姿勢が強まり、方向感の乏しい展開となった。ＡＩ（人工知能）・半導体関連株が売られた一方、決算など個別材料を手掛かりにした物色もみられた。

日経平均は前営業日比０．３９％安でスタートした後、プラス転換し、一時０．３３％（２０９円）高の６万２９０２円９５銭まで上昇した。ただ、買いの勢いは続かず上昇一服後は小幅安でもみ合った。ＡＩ関連株は売りが優勢だったものの、内需関連やバリュー（割安）株がしっかりで相場を支えた。原油価格の高止まりを受けてエネルギー関連株も堅調だった。

後場に入ると一段と様子見ムードが広がったが、大引けにかけてはやや売りが強まった。

市場では「ＡＩ・半導体株が調整含みとなる中、内需関連株が買われるという構図が続いている。指数のけん引役が不在のため、日経平均はもみ合いが続きそうだ」（岡三証券のシニアストラテジスト・大下莉奈氏）との声が聞かれた。注目度が高い国内のハイテク企業の決算については、「投資家の期待も高い分、ポジティブサプライズが出ないとなかなか買いが継続しにくい」（大下氏）という。

ＴＯＰＩＸは０．１８％高の３９７２．９８ポイントで取引を終えた。東証プライム市場指数は前営業日比０．１８％高の２０４７．４１ポイントだった。プライム市場の売買代金は６兆６４３８億５９００万円だった。東証３３業種では、東証３３業種では、鉱業、石油・石炭製品、卸売など２２業種が値上がり。非鉄金属、電機機器、証券、商品先物など１１業種が値下がりした。

新興株式市場では、東証グロース市場２５０指数が続伸し、１．１８％高の７６３．４９ポイントとなった。

個別では、豊田通商、三菱商事、伊藤忠商事など商社株が堅調に推移した。前週末に決算を発表したファナックは小幅高。一方、ＧＭＯインターネットグループが急落し１５％超安となった。

指数寄与度の高いアドバンテスト、東京エレクトロンは３％超安。キオクシアホールディングスも値下がりした。

東証プライム市場の騰落数は、値上がりが８１８銘柄（５２％）、値下がりは６８６銘柄（４４％）、変わらずは４９銘柄（３％）だった。

再送-東京外為市場・15時＝ドル157円付近で膠着、日米中銀会合控え積極的な取引手控え
10/26 16:02 配信

写真は１ドル紙幣。2021年11月撮影。REUTERS/Murad Sezer

(本文の表現を一部修正し、再送します。)

Atsuko Aoyama

[東京 ２６日 ロイター] -

  ドル／円 ユーロ／ドル ユーロ／円

午後３時現在 157.09／157.11 1.1216／1.1218 176.21／176.22

午前９時現在 156.83／156.84 1.1217／1.1218 175.92／175.93

ＮＹ午後５時 156.86／156.87 1.1202／1.1204 175.70／175.73

午後３時のドル／円は、前週末ニューヨーク市場終盤と比べややドル高／円安の１５７円付近で推移している。原油高などを背景にドル買い圧力は根強いものの、日米中銀の金融政策決定会合を控えて手控えムードとなる中で取引を一方向に傾ける動きは強まらず、狭いレンジでの膠着した値動きが続いた。

ドルは、１５７円前半と１５６円後半を行き来する値動きとなった。正午前に１５６．６６円でこの日の安値を付けた後は一転してドル買いが強まり、１５７円前半に切り返した。足元では１５７円付近でのもみ合いとなっている。

日米中銀会合を前に手控えムードも強く、原油価格や株式市場の動向をにらんで小幅に上下する相場が続きそうだとの声が聞かれた。ＡＩ（人工知能）関連企業の信用不安を背景とする株安で前週に広がったリスクオフ的な動きは足元で一服しているものの、懸念は引き続きくすぶっている。

特に、株安下での米長期金利低下だったため、「リスクオフの中でも金利差が縮小すると、円キャリー巻き戻しの円買いが出る」（外為どっとコム総合研究所の神田卓也シニア為替アナリスト）面があるとの指摘が出ている。

日米中銀会合では今月は据え置きが予想されており、次回１２月会合の利上げも日米ともに７割前後まで既に織り込まれている。会見などで今後の利上げに対するスタンスの違いが明らかになるとみられるが、「利上げ期待が高まっても買われる余地はそれほどなく、利上げ期待がより剥落する国の通貨が売られることになりそうだ」（神田氏）という。

items.title: Acciones y moneda de Brasil se hunden; reelección de Lula termina con racha alcista
items.author: Rodrigo Campos, Marcela Ayres, Karin Strohecker
items.creator: Rodrigo Campos, Marcela Ayres, Karin Strohecker
items.summary: Las acciones brasileñas y el real se hundieron el lunes tras la inesperada reelección del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, lo que provocó la disipación del optimismo inversor que había surgido tras el éxito de su rival de derecha en la primera vuelta electoral.
items.body:
Las acciones brasileñas y el real se hundieron el lunes tras la inesperada reelección del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, lo que provocó la disipación del optimismo inversor que había surgido tras el éxito de su rival de derecha en la primera vuelta electoral.
El real brasileño se depreció un 8,36% a 5,4066 unidades por dólar, tras registrar un descenso del 12% al inicio de la jornada, uno de los mayores movimientos registrados y llegando a cotizar por sobre las 5,60 unidades.
Mientras, el referencial bursátil (.BVSP) se desplomó preliminarmente un 13,43% a 177.539,81 puntos, en su mayor baja porcentual diaria desde marzo de 2020 y luego de perder más de un 16% en la sesión.
La oleada de ventas afectó también a los bonos soberanos brasileños en los mercados internacionales; los títulos a más largo plazo fueron los más perjudicados, con la deuda con vencimiento en 2056 cayendo alrededor de 2,5 centavos.
La bolsa brasileña detuvo sus operaciones durante 30 minutos después de que el índice de referencia Bovespa (.BVSP) cayera un 10% respecto a su cierre anterior, lo que activó el mecanismo de interrupción automática del mercado, informó en un comunicado B3, el operador bursátil.
Los "credit default swaps" (CDS) a cinco años de Brasil, un indicador del costo de asegurarse contra un impago soberano, subieron hasta los 151,67 puntos básicos, frente a los 120,21 puntos del cierre del viernes, según datos de S&P Global Market Intelligence.
Ante el desplome de los mercados brasileños, el Tesoro nacional canceló las subastas programadas de bonos gubernamentales, tanto los vinculados a la inflación como los de tasa fija, previstas para el 27 y el 29 de octubre, respectivamente.
El colapso supone un giro drástico respecto a la tendencia alcista este mes, cuando los mercados subieron ante la expectativa de un viraje hacia la derecha, después de que Flávio Bolsonaro, hijo del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro, obtuvo inesperadamente el primer lugar en la primera vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales.
El viernes, el índice Bovespa cerró casi un 7% por encima de su nivel previo a la primera vuelta, mientras que el real se había fortalecido cerca de un 5% frente al dólar. Los futuros de las tasas de interés también reflejaban la expectativa de que una política fiscal más restrictiva, bajo un eventual gobierno de Flávio Bolsonaro, permitiría una reducción en los costos de endeudamiento.
La negativa del senador Bolsonaro a reconocer su derrota y su promesa de buscar la anulación de los resultados han aumentado la incertidumbre entre los inversores.
"Un factor clave para los mercados financieros locales será la rapidez con la que Bolsonaro acepte el resultado, o al menos permita que el proceso constitucional siga su curso", afirmó Chris Turner, estratega de ING en Londres.
Ahora, la atención se centrará en la elección de Lula para el cargo de ministro de Hacienda y en lo que esto revele sobre su enfoque fiscal.
"La señal fundamental para los mercados será el compromiso de la futura administración de Lula con la disciplina fiscal, empezando por el nombramiento de un nuevo ministro de Hacienda en las próximas semanas", indicó Graham Stock, de RBC BlueBay Asset Management.
DESAFÍOS Lula se enfrenta al reto de frenar el aumento de la deuda de Brasil, al tiempo que protege los programas sociales y la inversión. Los inversores buscan indicios de que su enfoque fiscal gradualista pueda reducir los costos de endeudamiento.
"La administración de Lula no tendrá más remedio que llevar a cabo cierta consolidación fiscal, pero la mayoría de los inversores duda de que sea suficiente para encarrilar de nuevo la sostenibilidad de la deuda", comentó Thierry Larose, gestor de carteras en Vontobel Asset Management.
Si no existe la confianza de que Lula pueda cumplir sus objetivos, los prestamistas podrían exigir tipos de interés más elevados, lo que aumentaría la carga de la deuda brasileña y encarecería el crédito para empresas y hogares.
"Los inversionistas quieren un compromiso claro y creíble con la disciplina fiscal", dijo Alejo Czerwonko, director de inversiones para mercados emergentes de UBS Global Wealth Management. "Prevemos que el repunte que siguió a la primera vuelta ya esté en gran medida descontado en los precios, y que el ánimo se mantenga débil hasta que surja un plan fiscal claro".
Czerwonko señaló que los inversionistas esperan que se ponga fin al gasto que acompañó a la campaña y que se trace una vía creíble para estabilizar la deuda pública. "Esto también implica una relación de trabajo con un Congreso de tendencia opositora, ya que ningún plan fiscal se aprueba sin él", añadió.
El equipo de Lula se propone alcanzar un superávit presupuestario primario de alrededor del 1,3% del producto interno bruto para 2030. Eso dejaría fondos para cubrir parte de los intereses, reduciendo la necesidad de nuevos préstamos. Sin embargo, la deuda pública ya supera el 82% del PIB, mientras que las pensiones y otros gastos obligatorios por ley limitan las fuentes de ahorro.
"Las políticas de Lula han hablado de recortes de gasto, pero no ha entrado en detalles sobre cómo se concretarán", señaló Divya Singaravelu, directora de investigación de Meridian 1305 Capital.

items.body:
US STOCKS-Wall St set for higher open as Anthropic's IPO filing sharpens AI focus
Reuters | Updated: 26-10-2026 18:45 IST | Created: 26-10-2026 18:45 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US stocks were set to open higher on Monday as Anthropic's IPO filing drew investor attention ahead of a week dominated by corporate earnings and the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision. Anthropic laid out its ambitions to build AI systems capable of transforming the global economy while confronting the costs and challenges of developing the technology.
The company is pressing ahead with its IPO plans even as a once-busy fall listing calendar has thinned out, with market volatility prompting companies to delay offerings. Most megacap and growth stocks moved higher in premarket trading, with Tesla gaining 2.5% after Barclays upgraded its rating on the stock to "overweight" from "equal-weight".
Semiconductor and chip-related companies also climbed after a turbulent few weeks. Nvidia and rivals AMD and Intel all rose more than 1% each. At 09:05 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 208 points, or 0.4%, S&P 500 E-minis were up 25.75 points, or 0.34%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 175.5 points, or 0.6%.
About a third of S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report earnings this week, including hyperscalers Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon.com, whose results would be closely watched for signs that hefty AI investments are paying off. The focus follows a muted reception to earnings from AI-linked megacaps last week. Meta disappointed investors after raising its annual AI spending forecast again and said it would sell new stock to help pay for it, while Tesla also came under pressure after its results.
"It does feel like in this earning season that companies are trapped now, because if you spend too much that's a concern for investors, but then if you signal you're not spending enough, then investors start to worry as well," said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG Group. Meta said on Monday it plans to raise up to $95 billion in equity to fund its AI-related expansion of data centers, cloud computing power and other infrastructure. Its shares were last down 0.7%.
The AI trade has come under pressure this month amid concerns that debt-funded spending may become harder to justify in the face of rising borrowing costs. Neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius have each lost more than 30% of their market value in October. CoreWeave fell 3.9% and Nebius dipped 1.7% after Elon Musk said in an X post markets have "almost entirely shut off access to money" for companies without substantial revenue independent of AI data centers, and predicted neocloud consolidation.
Musk also said SpaceX would not buy any neocloud firms, calling that "pointless". IREN and Applied Digital also dropped slightly. Crude oil prices eased after hitting a near six-month high last week. On Sunday, Qatari mediators traveled to Tehran as part of an effort to de-escalate regional tensions in coordination with the United States.
EYES ON THE FED AND MIDTERMS The Fed's rate decision is due on Wednesday, with a pause widely expected after its September hike. Traders still see a December hike as firmly possible, and at least two 25-basis-point increases by mid-2027, according to LSEG data.
Both the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the Personal Consumption Expenditures index for September, and third-quarter GDP, expected to show 3.2% growth, are due on Thursday. Investors are also monitoring the November 3 midterm elections, which will decide control of the US Congress.
Among other movers, US-listed shares of Brazilian companies tumbled after President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a historic fourth term on Sunday, in a shock result that defied polls. The iShares Brazil ETF slumped over 26%.

items.summary: Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church on Friday, killing nine people and wounding 40 others.

Jordan arrests three suspects in deadly church attack

Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church on Friday, killing nine people and wounding 40 others.

FAST

Jordanian security forces have arrested three suspects in connection with an attack on a church in the US-allied country that killed nine people, state television reported on Monday (Oct 26). 
The attack, in which gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church on Friday in the village of Hamoud in Karak governorate, about 120 km southwest of the capital Amman, also wounded 40 others. The shooting lasted several minutes, witnesses said.
Jordan's Public Security Directorate said security forces located the three suspects early on Monday hiding in an abandoned house in Karak. The suspects refused to surrender and opened fire on security forces, who returned fire and arrested all three after they were wounded, the directorate said in a statement carried on state media.
No security personnel were injured, and a number of firearms and ammunition were found in the suspects' possession after their arrest.
"Terrorism has no place among us," the directorate said, adding that the suspects had met their "just fate".
The Public Security Directorate did not identify the suspects' affiliation or say whether they belonged to any militant group.

The grounds of Saint George’s Greek Orthodox Church, where gunmen opened fire during a funeral the previous day, is cordoned-off, in the village of Hamoud, Karak, Jordan, October 24, 2026. REUTERS/Alaa Al Sukhni

Jordanian authorities have said the attack was carried out by "extremist terrorists", but it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan. There has been no claim of responsibility.
Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said on Monday authorities were reviewing the circumstances that led young people towards extremism and would hold accountable anyone found to have participated in the attack.
King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against Islamist militant groups, has ordered security forces to respond with an "iron fist" to the rare attack on Jordan's Christian minority.
Such violence is highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable state in the Middle East, though authorities say they have foiled several Islamist militant plots over the years.

items.title: Brazil stocks, real tumble as Lula win shifts investor focus
items.author: Rodrigo Campos, Marcela Ayres, Karin Strohecker
items.creator: Rodrigo Campos, Marcela Ayres, Karin Strohecker
items.summary: Brazilian stocks and the real currency posted their sharpest losses in years on Monday after the surprise reelection of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva reversed recent market bets on a right-wing ascent to power.
items.body:
Brazilian stocks and the real currency posted their sharpest losses in years on Monday after the surprise [USN:L6N4681ER TEXT:"reelection"] of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva reversed recent market bets on a right-wing ascent to power.
Brazil's real , tumbled over 11% against the US dollar in early spot trading, one of its biggest intraday declines on record, while the benchmark Bovespa stock index (.BVSP) closed down 13.9% in its largest daily percentage drop since March 2020.
The selloff also hit [USN:L5N46C0GQ TEXT:"sovereign debt"], with longer-dated bonds hit hardest and the 2054 maturity down 2.2 cents to yield 7.45% as Brazil's fiscal path came into focus.
"Lula’s victory triggered a sharp market selloff as investors reassessed the fiscal outlook under his fourth term,” Mauricio Monge, senior Latin America economist at Oxford Economics, said in a report.
His biggest challenge, Monge wrote, "will be to convince markets that he can deliver a credible, sustainable fiscal adjustment while prioritizing real wage growth and employment."
TRADING HALTED Trading on Brazil's stock exchange was halted for 30 minutes after the Bovespa index fell 10% from its last close, triggering the market's circuit breaker mechanism, stock exchange operator B3 said in a statement. Earlier, B3 expanded the daily trading limits for Bovespa stock index futures, dollar futures and interest rate futures in response to heightened volatility.
Brazil's five-year credit default swaps, a measure of the cost of insuring against sovereign default, jumped to 144 basis points from Friday's close of 120 bps, S&P Global Market Intelligence data showed.
As markets tumbled, the Brazilian Treasury cancelled its regular auctions of inflation-linked and fixed-rate government bonds scheduled for October 27 and October 29, respectively.
The real was down 8.1% to the dollar at 5.415 per greenback for its largest daily drop since at least 2002. Prices of raw sugar, of which Brazil is a major exporter, slid 5.6% on the collapsing exchange rate.
The plunge is a sharp reversal from the rally earlier this month, when markets soared on expectations of a shift to the right after Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, unexpectedly finished first in the opening round of Brazil's presidential elections.
The Bovespa closed on Friday almost 7% above its level before the first-round vote, while the real currency had been nearly 5% stronger against the US dollar over that period. Interest rate futures had also reflected expectations that tighter fiscal policy under a Bolsonaro government would make room for lower borrowing costs.
Senator Bolsonaro's refusal to concede and his pledge to seek an annulment added to investor uncertainty.
"Important for local financial markets will be how quickly Bolsonaro accepts the result, or at least allows the constitution to run its course," said Chris Turner, strategist at ING in London.
CHALLENGES AHEAD Attention will now turn to Lula's choice of finance minister and what it signals about his fiscal approach.
"The key signal for markets will be the next Lula administration's commitment to fiscal discipline, starting with the appointment of a new finance minister in coming weeks," said Graham Stock at RBC BlueBay Asset Management.
Lula faces the [USN:L1N468127 TEXT:"challenge"] of slowing the rise in Brazil's debt while protecting social programmes and investment, with investors looking for signs his gradual fiscal approach can lower borrowing costs.
"The more the fiscal pressures build, the more we see the debt burden rise without any clear, credible fiscal plan to bring deficits down over the longer term, that would start to raise more and more potential pressures for a change in the (credit rating) outlook to negative," said William Foster, senior vice president for sovereign ratings at Moody's and its lead Brazil analyst.
Moody's rates Brazil's external sovereign debt Ba1, one level below investment grade, with a stable outlook.
Without confidence that Lula can deliver, lenders could demand higher interest rates, adding to Brazil's debt burden and making credit more expensive for businesses and households.
"Investors want a clear and credible commitment to fiscal discipline," said Alejo Czerwonko, chief investment officer for emerging markets at UBS Global Wealth Management.
"We expect the rally that followed the first round to be largely priced out, and sentiment to stay weak until a clear fiscal plan emerges," Czerwonko said, adding that investors wanted a believable path to stabilize public debt.
The reelected president's team has said it aims to produce a budget surplus of about 1.3% of gross domestic product by 2030.
"Lula's policies have talked about spending cuts," said Divya Singaravelu, head of research at Meridian 1305 Capital, "but he has not gone into the details of how that is going to look."

items.title: Jordan says its air force struck 'militant hideouts' in Syria after church attack
items.author: Abdelhadi Ramahi, Yasmine Ghania, Muhammad Gebaly
items.creator: Abdelhadi Ramahi, Yasmine Ghania, Muhammad Gebaly
items.summary: Jordan said on Monday its air force struck what it described as militant hideouts in southern Syria after determining that the suspects behind last week's deadly church attack in the kingdom were linked to "terrorist groups" operating there.
items.body:
Jordan said on Monday its air force struck what it described as militant hideouts in southern Syria after determining that the suspects behind last week's deadly church attack in the kingdom were linked to "terrorist groups" operating there.
The armed forces said the operation was conducted in coordination with Damascus. Syria's government gave a contradictory account, saying it had launched an investigation into the Jordanian attacks, and stressed in a statement the importance of field and security coordination in border areas.
Damascus informed Jordan of its "complete reservation" over the strikes without prior coordination, the foreign ministry said in a statement.
Seven people, including three children and a woman, were killed and three others were wounded in the Jordanian strikes, the Syrian Civil Defence said in a preliminary report. It said emergency teams responded to four sites hit by the strikes in the countryside of Daraa and Sweida provinces.
There was no immediate comment from Jordan on that account.
Shortly after the strikes, Syria closed the Nassib border crossing with Jordan on Tuesday, suspending passenger and commercial traffic in both directions, citing developments on the ground in Daraa province, the Syrian General Authority for Border Crossings and Customs said in a statement.
Nassib is Jordan's only passenger and commercial border crossing with Syria.
Earlier on Monday, senior government security officials said Jordanian security forces had arrested two brothers and their brother-in-law after a shootout on Monday over the church violence that killed nine people.
"God willing, they only represent themselves," said Jordan's Director of Public Security, Major-General Obeidallah al-Maaytah.
Such violence is rare in Jordan, a relatively stable US ally in the Middle East. Friday's attack on the Christian minority prompted King Abdullah to order security forces to respond with an "iron fist".
In a press conference, al-Maaytah and Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said the country would not tolerate extremist terrorism.
"The file has not yet been closed; investigations are still ongoing. As of today, there are no indications of any links between them and other cells," al-Faraya added.
ATTACK TARGETED GREEK ORTHODOX FUNERAL Friday's assault during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hamoud, about 120 km (75 miles) southwest of the capital, Amman, also wounded at least 34 people. [USN:L6N46B02Q TEXT:"Witnesses"] said gunmen opened fire for several minutes. The suspects, who lived near Hamoud, will face justice, said the security officials. The three suspects were named in the press briefing.
Reuters video footage showed a building pockmarked by the exchange of fire in the village of al-Judayyda, in Karak governorate.
Jordan's Public Security Directorate said in a statement carried by state media that security forces located the suspects while they were hiding in an abandoned house. They refused to surrender and attacked security forces, who returned fire and arrested all three after wounding them.
No security personnel were injured, and security forces found a number of firearms and rounds of ammunition in the suspects' possession.
There has been no claim of responsibility for the church attack.
Jordan, a US partner in the fight against extremism, has foiled Islamist militant plots in the past. The security officials did not name any Islamist groups in the press conference.
